Title: Nvidia shares slide 8pct as doubts persist over Huang's return
Article:
WASHINGTON: A rally sparked by Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's chief executive faded on Tuesday, with the company's shares falling as doubts persisted over the probes he faces and the fate of the AI investment boom.
"The optimism faded quickly" for Nvidia, wrote Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com, with "questions over corporate governance and board oversight still lingering."
After vaulting more than 30  per cent on Monday following Huang's shock comeback as CEO, Nvidia was down about eight  per cent Tuesday.
"This could be a 'one day wonder' and so far it is since we are not seeing an upside follow through today at all," said Ken Mahoney, president and CEO of Mahoney Asset Management.
Huang resigned on Nov 12 over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in Nvidia and companies closely linked to the AI buildout tumbling.
The rescue of the Taiwan-born Huang was orchestrated by US President Donald Trump, who, according to reports, was talked into advocating for the CEO's return after top tech investors told him the US economy and stability on Wall Street depended on it.
Nvidia said Monday that it had reinstated Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.
Trump is also an investor in Nvidia, owning as many as 370,000 shares in the company as of Sept 30, according to filings.
The stock market in recent weeks has seen massive falls in shares linked to the AI boom, with fears growing that the AI bubble was finally coming to an end after four years of bullish growth sparked by the launch of ChatGPT in 2022.
In bearish markets, quick rebounds are common but "tend to get negated and that has been the sequence since early October," Mahoney said, adding that "sellers have absolute control of the market here."
Nvidia is central to the AI investment story – its powerful processors are the key tool to train and run the AI models that are believed to be at the heart of a technological revolution.
The massive spending on its AI chips and software, housed in sprawling data centres, catapulted the company into the ranks of the world's most valuable firms.
Huang used that success to turn Nvidia into a kind of central bank for other AI companies and startups, generously doling out loans and financial backstops to firms that would otherwise struggle to find easy financing from traditional lenders.
The departure of the leather jacket-wearing CEO had thrown the AI economy into doubt, and his return seemed to inject confidence back into the AI trade on Monday, before fizzling out again on Tuesday.
- LEGAL BATTLES -
Investors are also weighing a barrage of legal challenges facing Huang and Nvidia.
The board that let Huang go and then rehired him is still overseeing an internal investigation into concerns that he may have been the target of a Chinese espionage campaign, even though Trump says he has been cleared.
The Justice Department is separately investigating Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that allegedly bought Nvidia processors and routed them to Chinese customers in violation of US export restrictions.
The Securities and Exchange Commission has also reportedly opened a probe into Nvidia's accounting practices and potentially misleading communication to shareholders.
The Trump administration has generally avoided going after its allies, so the federal probes may not amount to much, said Columbia University professor Eric Talley.
Huang will nevertheless face lawmakers at a closed-door hearing before three House committees on Dec 1 and a livestreamed Senate committee hearing on Dec 3.
Lawmakers from both parties have expressed anger over the circumstances of Huang's return, and the scrutiny is likely to intensify in January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress after sweeping this month's midterm elections.
California's attorney general has also opened an investigation into the company's chip exports and shareholder disclosures.
"We all have an opportunity to enforce laws, and I would say a duty, especially if other entities, like the federal government in my humble opinion, are not," California Attorney General Rob Bonta told CNBC.--AFP

Title: PKR not contesting Sarawak election due to political consensus with GPS
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak PKR has decided not to contest in the 13th state election as a sign of respect for the spirit of cooperation and political consensus with Gabungan Parti Sarawak.
The decision was announced today via a joint statement by three state party leaders: adviser Datuk Seri Hafsah Harun, PKR vice-resident Roland Engan, and Sarawak PKR leadership council chairman Mahmud Epah.
"The main consideration underlying this stance is as a sign of respect for the spirit of cooperation, consensus, and political commitment within the unity government to preserve political stability at the state and federal levels," the statement read.
The decision also aims to strengthen the cooperative relationship between the federal government and the Sarawak government, particularly in implementing the demands of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
It is also meant to ensure that Sarawak's development agenda, economic progress and the well-being of its people continue to receive due attention.
Sarawak PKR also expressed its commitment to continue upholding democratic principles, the reform agenda and social justice, prioritising the people's welfare, and maintaining the political understanding built with GPS.
The state leadership council has instructed the entire party machinery and leadership at all levels in the state to abide by and respect the decision.
They were also asked to continue maintaining good relations with component partners in the unity government, particularly GPS.
"Sarawak PKR will continue to fulfill its responsibilities and serve the people of Sarawak without neglecting its role in the state," the joint statement added.
The Election Commission has set Dec 12 as polling day for the election, nomination day on Nov 28, and early voting on Dec 8. - BERNAMA

Title: 'Hopes of 250 million' for Pakistani on China space mission
Article:
THE first foreign astronaut on a Chinese space mission said on Tuesday that he will be carrying 'the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis' when he blasts off from the Gobi Desert this week.
Beijing has poured billions into the Chinese space programme, whose prized Tiangong space station is stewarded by teams of three astronauts, typically rotated every six months.
The Shenzhou-24 mission is set to lift off at 8.18 am (0018 GMT) on Wednesday from the Jiuquan launch centre in northwest China, China Manned Space Agency spokesman Zhang Jingbo told a news conference.
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistan Air Force pilot and payload specialist, will be the first foreign astronaut to fly on a Chinese space mission and also the first non-Chinese to board the Tiangong space station.
"I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis," Ali told a separate news conference held later on Tuesday to introduce the crew.
"To every child who is watching while I'm in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams," he said in English, following other remarks in Urdu and Mandarin.
Ali will join a short orbital flight expected to last around five days before returning with the Shenzhou-23 spaceship, which docked at the Tiangong space station in May.
Pakistan's space agency said Ali would conduct experiments in orbit, including cultivating microalgae as a potential food and oxygen source for future space missions, and testing the effects of spaceflight on quinoa seeds.
Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif hailed the mission as a testament to the "exceptional trust, mutual respect and enduring brotherhood" between the two countries.
"Pakistan-China friendship is surpassing the heights of the Himalayas, in its journey to outer space," he said.
[[nid:1585098]]
Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing that 'China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners.'
Pakistan's Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who is in China for the launch, said the mission underscored the trust and 'iron brotherhood' between the two countries.
China was excluded from the International Space Station in 2011 when the United States banned NASA from collaborating with Beijing.
This prompted the Asian giant to invest heavily in its own space activities, landing a probe on the far side of the Moon in 2019 and a rover on Mars in 2021.
China successfully landed a reusable rocket for the first time in July, according to its space agency, marking a major step in its space ambitions and in reducing launch costs.
China is aiming to land astronauts on the Moon before 2030, a race in which the United States is also competing with its Artemis programme.
The crew currently aboard the Tiangong space station is headed by 40-year-old Zhu Yangzhu, Lai Ka-ying and Zhang Zhiyuan, also 40.
Lai is Hong Kong's first astronaut and the only woman currently aboard.
After the new, all-male crew reaches the Tiangong, Pakistan's Ali will return to Earth alongside Lai and Zhang.
Zhu will remain on board to complete China's first full-year stay in space – a key test of endurance critical for future lunar and potentially deep-space ambitions.
Zhu will be accompanied for the next six-month Tiangong rotation by 51-year-old space veteran Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, in his late thirties and making his first voyage to space.
Ali is not the first Pakistani in space, with Monaco-based polar adventurer Namira Salim having flown on Virgin Galactic's Galactic 04 mission in October 2023.
* The writer is from AFP

Title: Falling oil prices mask stubborn global diesel shortage
Article:
NINE  months into the biggest energy shock in modern history, the oil market's recovery is surprisingly swift, but plentiful crude supplies are masking a stubborn diesel shortage that could yet upend fuel markets.
Benchmark Brent crude has dropped by more than 20 per cent since the start of the month to just over US$90 a barrel.
Recovering Middle East exports and fading fears of a major escalation in the United States-Iran war have driven the decline.
The retreat comes after high fuel prices pummelled US President Donald Trump's Republican Party in this month's midterm elections.
Crucially, petrol and diesel prices have also retreated from their peaks, offering consumers some relief and promising to ease inflationary pressures on governments.
In Europe, a major diesel importer, futures prices have fallen by a quarter from their September peak to around US$160 a barrel, but they remain nearly twice their level at the start of the year.
In the US, the world's largest refiner and oil consumer, retail diesel prices have slipped below US$6 to a two-month low, while petrol was down below US$4 for the first time since August, according to GasBuddy.
Any lasting recovery hinges on easing Middle East tensions, however, and that is far from assured.
Iran has stepped up attacks on tankers around the Strait of Hormuz and struck facilities in Bahrain and Kuwait, while Yemen's Houthi militia continues to target Saudi Arabia.
As a result, oil flows through Hormuz slowed to around 9.5 million barrels per day (bpd) in the 10 days through Nov 19, from an average of 12.2 million bpd last month, which was the highest level since the war began in late February, according to shipping analytics firm Kpler.
The Middle East disruption has resulted in the loss of nearly three billion barrels of oil, more than any previous crisis, forcing consumers to draw heavily on inventories, which have fallen by a cumulative 462 million barrels since the start of the war, according to the International Energy Agency. Recovering Middle East exports have begun to close that gap.
Commercial US crude stockpiles have risen by around two per cent since the start of this month after hitting their lowest point since 2018 in September.
China also appeared to add to its vast crude inventories last month.
Crude, in other words, is no longer the market's biggest headache.
Fuel markets remain considerably tighter. The tightness, though, is tilted heavily towards diesel following the loss of refining capacity in the Middle East and months of Ukrainian attacks on Russian infrastructure.
Last year, the Middle East and Russia together accounted for more than two million bpd, or nearly 30 per cent, of the 7.4 million bpd of diesel shipped by sea.
Global seaborne diesel exports have averaged just 6.2 million bpd so far this year despite sharply higher US shipments, explaining why diesel remains scarce.
Petrol tells a very different story. The market has been far less exposed to the loss of Middle Eastern and Russian supplies, allowing inventories to recover much faster.
US petrol margins of around US$20 a barrel are back below their pre-war levels.
European diesel refining margins have similarly retreated from around US$90 a barrel in September to US$60, but they remain roughly triple their 2025 average.
Falling product prices have also sharply reduced US refining profitability. The benchmark US refining crack spread has dropped from a record US$72 a barrel in September to around US$41 now.
That leaves refiners caught in an unusual bind: running hard to capture strong diesel margins, they are simultaneously pumping more petrol into a market that is already recovering quickly.
For now, diesel's extraordinary profitability should comfortably compensate refiners for weaker petrol returns. And with global fuel inventories still diminished after nine months of disruption, petrol prices are unlikely to collapse.
However, if petrol supplies build far enough to crush margins, they could eventually overwhelm diesel's profitability and drag overall refining margins toward levels that force plants to cut runs.
For now, that remains a distant prospect. But until all product markets come back into balance, unexpected price anomalies will likely continue popping up.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: Imam freed of sexual assault charges involving disabled girl
Article:
AYER KEROH: The High Court here today acquitted and discharged an imam of physical and non-physical sexual assault charges involving a 13-year-old girl with an intellectual disability at a surau storeroom in Limbongan four years ago.
Judge Datuk DJP Suria Kumar allowed the appeal by Ashar Sabtuawan, 63, and set aside the conviction and sentences imposed by the Sessions Court.
The Sessions Court had convicted Ashar on June 10 last year and sentenced him to nine years' jail and three strokes of the rotan for the first charge, and three years' jail for the second charge, with the sentences to run concurrently.
In allowing the appeal, Suria said the court found significant inconsistencies between the victim's oral testimony and the transcript of her interview at the Child Interview Centre (CIC), particularly over the presence of another child witness.
He said the victim had also agreed during cross-examination with the defence's suggestions that Ashar had not pulled her into the surau storeroom, touched her or removed his clothes and sarong in front of her.
The victim had said there was a communal gathering for a Hari Raya feast on the day of the incident.
During re-examination by the deputy public prosecutor, however, she failed to explain why she had agreed with the defence's suggestions and remained silent, the judge said.
"The court hereby sets aside the conviction and sentences imposed by the Sessions Court judge. The accused is acquitted and discharged of both charges. The bail money is to be returned," he said.
Ashar was charged under Sections 14(a) and 15(1)(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Azfar Mahmod prosecuted, while Ashar was represented by lawyer Mohd Yusoff AG Lah.
The prosecution had argued that the Sessions Court's conviction and sentences were safe and legally sound, and should be upheld.
Speaking to reporters after the hearing, Ashar expressed gratitude over his acquittal after four years of court proceedings.

Title: Saudi Arabia's tallest skyscraper hit again in suspected Houthi attack, 11 injured
Article:
RIYADH: The Saudi capital's tallest skyscraper was struck for the second time in days on Tuesday, witnesses said, injuring 11 people, as the coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis denounced a "terrorist attack."
Three separate witnesses said the strike targeted the 80-storey Public Investment Fund Tower, which houses the kingdom's sovereign wealth fund and dominates Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD).
The building, which was also attacked last Thursday, is one of several high-profile targets hit since hostilities with the Iran-backed Houthis restarted in July.
"One of the towers in the financial centre was targeted in a cowardly terrorist attack," coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said in a social media post, without naming the building.
"The relevant authorities are currently inspecting the attack site."
Saudi Arabia's civil defence later said 11 people were injured in the attack it blamed on the Houthis.
"The attack resulted in 11 people being injured," read a report by the Saudi Press Agency, saying Indian, Nepali and Egyptian nationals along with Saudi citizens were among those wounded.
A source briefed on the details of the attack told AFP that several people were in the tower repairing the damage caused by last week's attack when the building was struck again Tuesday.
The source said at least two of the 11 injured were in critical condition after sustaining severe burns during the strike.
An attack on the PIF is symbolic as the fund is driving efforts to diversify the oil-reliant Saudi economy – a project that has been complicated by the Middle East war and Houthi strikes.
A tower belonging to state oil giant Aramco in KAFD was hit earlier this month, while Riyadh's international airport was repeatedly struck in October with one attack killing 14 people.
A fourth witness told AFP a vehicle fitted with a speaker had warned pedestrians in the area to take cover on Tuesday. No warning was sent to mobile phones about any threats to the capital.
Afterwards, police cars blocked some entrances to the gleaming financial district, a showpiece of Saudi Arabia's modernisation under Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the de facto ruler.
A waiter at a KAFD restaurant told AFP: "We just reopened a while ago.
"They evacuated all of us telling us a tower has been hit. They closed the streets and they banned people from passing in streets or entering."
- WEEKS OF VIOLENCE -
Last week, Saudi officials said an attack on a tower in the financial district damaged several floors and two adjacent buildings but caused no casualties.
Although authorities did not identify the building, photos released by the civil defence agency appeared to show shattered glass and other exterior damage to the PIF tower.
The Houthis claimed responsibility for last week's attack, but they did not announce any fresh attacks on Tuesday.
Standing 385 metres high, the PIF tower is the most prominent landmark of KAFD, a showcase for Saudi Arabia's economic ambitions.
With imposing skyscrapers, luxury shops and green spaces, the district also hosts the headquarters of the Saudi stock exchange along with multinationals such as Goldman Sachs.
The Houthis have stepped up their attacks against Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, striking military, civilian and oil infrastructure.
The major attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport forced the suspension of flights for two weeks. Several events have been cancelled, including the Future Investment Initiative financial conference, dubbed "Davos in the desert."
In response, a Saudi-led military coalition fighting on behalf of Yemen's government has been striking Houthi targets in the impoverished country.
On Tuesday, local officials said a coalition airstrike on buses and trucks killed 26 people in Lahj province. Government forces blamed the Houthis for the attack.
As the conflict shows no sign of slowing, Britain sanctioned the Houthis and four of its top officials "for deliberately attempting to undermine stability" on Tuesday.
The measures include an asset freeze against the group and an asset freeze and travel ban on four figures, including security and intelligence head Abdul Hakim Hashem Ali al-Khaiwani, and interior affairs official Abdulkarim Amir al-Din Hussein al-Houthi.
The Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen in early 2015, after the Houthis had captured the capital Sanaa and sent the internationally recognised government fleeing to Aden.
The war left hundreds of thousands dead and triggered a humanitarian catastrophe before an uneasy ceasefire went into effect in 2022.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UK police arrest two men after break-in at William and Kate's home
Article:
LONDON: Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary, police said on Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the countryside retreat of UK royals Prince William and his wife Catherine, who were not in residence at the time.
Police dogs, drones and a helicopter were deployed to the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, eastern England, after the local force received a call just before 6 pm (1800 GMT) on Monday of 'suspicious activity', Norfolk police said in a statement sent to AFP.
Anmer Hall where William, Kate and their three children occasionally live – especially during the school holidays – was broken into, according to UK media.
The 10-bedroom red-brick Georgian manor was gifted to the couple by the late Queen Elizabeth II after their marriage.
The men "were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass", police said.
The sprawling Sandringham estate is owned by William's father King Charles.
Police said the property 'was unoccupied' at the time and the men remained in custody.
William and Kate mainly live at their home on the Windsor estate, just west of London.
Kensington Palace, which handles the affairs of William, the heir to the throne, did not immediately reply to AFP's request for comment.
Charles's disgraced brother, the former prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, moved to Sandringham earlier this year and lives about a mile from Anmer Hall.
The king ousted Andrew from his home of two decades in Windsor and stripped him of his royal titles amid the fallout from his brother's alleged dealings with the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
It is not the first time a royal residence has been broken into, despite the tight security surrounding the royal family.
In 2024, several intruders were caught on the Windsor estate after they broke into a farm building and tried to steal a pick-up truck and a quad bike.
In Christmas 2021, a 21-year-old man with mental health issues was arrested after being caught near the queen's apartments armed with a loaded crossbow.
He admitted in court to trying to kill Elizabeth and was handed a nine-year sentence, to be served initially in the high-security Broadmoor psychiatric hospital.
The most famous incident was in July 1982, when a man named Michael Fagan sneaked into Buckingham Palace and made his way to Queen Elizabeth II's bedroom.
He sat on her four-poster bed and had a 10-minute chat with her before being taken away by security. He was initially charged but the accusations were later dropped.
News of Monday's break-in came just as William made his first visit to Downing Street, where he talked about 'shared priorities' with Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
The meeting was seen as another step towards the heir to the throne's future role as monarch.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Pak Samad often sent me letters, his literary works while I was in prison
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri A. Samad Said often wrote letters and sent his literary works to Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim while the latter was serving his sentence at Sungai Buloh Prison.
The prime minister said their friendship, which began in 1998, reflected the late writer's thoughtfulness, as he regularly ensured that Anwar received his literary works and shared his thoughts through letters.
He said Samad, affectionately known as Pak Samad, was a towering national figure who not only championed the arts and literature but also played an important role in educating the nation.
"He was a dedicated person, a lover of the arts and literature, and an educator who shaped the nation. The country has certainly lost a great national laureate," he said after paying his last respects at the Saidina Abu Bakar As-Siddiq mosque in Bangsar.
Present was Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Anwar said Samad's works had begun gaining public recognition as early as 1955, underscoring his significant contributions to the development of the country's literary scene.
He said one of the qualities that could inspire the younger generation was Samad's dedication to championing language and literature as essential elements of life and nation-building.
"He firmly believed that literature was not an exclusive field that only certain groups needed to master, but should instead be part of a nation's strength.
"He was determined to uphold his love for language and literature, believing that literature should be mastered by all, rather than being regarded as a specialised field, as some people perceive it to be.
"The life of a nation and the building of its civilisation must also be underpinned by the strength of literature," he said.
Commenting on Samad's personality, Anwar said he had never encountered anyone as dedicated to reading as the national laureate, based on his observations of the collection of books and notes left behind at his residence.
He said each book read by the late writer contained his own annotations, reflecting his dedication to acquiring knowledge and exploring literature from various perspectives.
"His knowledge and mastery, particularly in the field of literature, will not be easily matched. Therefore, efforts to elevate the standing of national laureates must continue to receive attention," he said.
Samad
died at Kuala Lumpur Hospital
(HKL) about 6.05pm. He was 91.
The news was confirmed by his second son, Helmy Abdul Samad, in a post on Threads.
Samad had been receiving treatment at HKL after being admitted yesterday evening due to age-related ailments, diabetes and a lung infection.

Title: Jensen Huang's return lifts Nvidia, but AI doubts linger
Article:
FOR United States stock investors, Monday's stunning return of Nvidia chief executive officer (CEO) Jensen Huang brought a sigh of relief for the battered artificial intelligence (AI) trade, one worth trillions of dollars in market value.
Huang's reinstatement atop the semiconductor giant halted a severe slide in technology shares that had sent the benchmark S&P 500 into a correction amid growing doubts about the AI trade that had been the primary engine for the four-year-old bull stock market.
The reversal by Nvidia's board in bringing back Huang came after his abrupt departure earlier this month rattled an already anxious market.
Concerns flared not only about Nvidia, but also about the health of the AI ecosystem, which the chip company has been at the centre of.
"You've basically had this perfect storm of uncertainty that has created a crisis of confidence," said King Lip, chief strategist at BakerAvenue Wealth Management in San Francisco.
"This Nvidia fallout was one of those pieces of... uncertainty. So this removes a pretty significant one with Jensen coming back."
Shares of Nvidia soared on news of Huang's return to the company he co-founded, rising 32 per cent in early afternoon trading, equivalent to more than US$900 billion in market capitalisation added back to the value of the semiconductor company, whose stock price has been hammered in recent weeks.
Shares of companies across the AI industry rallied sharply, with the Nasdaq 100 that is concentrated in megacap tech companies jumping more than six per cent.
"The initial reaction here is a big collective sigh of relief," said Thomas Urano, co-chief investment officer at Sage Advisory in Austin, Texas.
"Maybe Jensen... puts confidence back in the AI trade."
Many investors had worried about the extent to which Nvidia's massive value was tied up in Huang, who was credited for foreseeing the technology shift that led to Nvidia's advanced chips that are central to the AI boom and to Nvidia's soaring profits.
Nvidia chief financial officer Colette Kress had been running the company on an interim basis while the company searched for a permanent replacement.
"To try to replace Jensen was something that nobody could feel comfortable that they are going to find somebody to automatically fill his shoes," said Tom Plumb, portfolio manager of the Plumb Balanced Fund in Madison, Wisconsin.
"But to have the visionary who was able to attract some of the most talented people in the industry... it's certainly very, very positive for the company."
Huang has been "essentially the product manager of his company", said Kim Forrest, chief investment officer at Bokeh Capital Partners.
"And that's really important, which is why a lot of investors are happy to see him back."
More broadly, Nvidia has been tied to an array of companies involved in the sprawling AI buildout.
Many investors had voiced concerns about the future of that ecosystem without Huang himself, who is seen as one of the most pivotal AI figures.
Some investors also said Huang's return could clear some regulatory clouds over the stock.
Huang's resignation followed revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China.
President Donald Trump, who said he secured the deal to bring back Huang, said in a post on Truth Social the US government had no reason to believe Huang's return posed a national security risk and had no evidence he had engaged in unlawful conduct.
Trump told CNBC that the stock market reaction to Huang's resignation from Nvidia "probably" factored into his decision to push for the CEO's reinstatement although his view of the long-term benefit of having Huang at the helm of the company was the bigger weight.
Some regulatory clouds could remain. California's attorney-general's office said on Monday Huang's reinstatement does not diminish the need for a probe into what Nvidia told investors about its China ties.
And questions about the AI trade that had dogged the market before the Nvidia crisis erupted were likely to persist.
"We very well may see more selling pressure after this relief rally runs its course," said James St. Aubin, chief investment officer at Ocean Park Asset Management in Santa Monica, California.
"Jensen's return doesn't answer the big questions investors were grappling with."
The writers are from Reuters

Title: UNHCR cardholders to be placed in third countries after transit, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cardholders will be placed in third countries after completing the transit stage, subject to the receiving countries' requirements and capacity, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said the arrangement was in line with the government's commitment to upholding human rights.
However, he said the process depended entirely on receiving countries, which determined the conditions and number of UNHCR cardholders they would accept at any one time.
"Malaysia's border control measures now went beyond physical barriers, with the use of modern technology including artificial intelligence (AI), drones and smart surveillance systems.
"The government would also take firm action against Malaysians who enabled foreigners to commit offences in the country, including those operating businesses without licences or local authority approval, as well as land or premises owners who allowed such activities."
He said this in a written parliamentary reply to Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar), who asked about the government's position on curbing refugee arrivals and UNHCR's follow-up action after the transit stage.
Earlier, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said 227,414 refugees and asylum seekers were registered with UNHCR in Malaysia as at Sept 30.
Of the total, 205,273, or 90.2 per cent, were from Myanmar, including 132,400 Rohingya.
Selangor recorded the highest number of UNHCR cardholders at 74,028, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 47,333 and Penang with 25,357.

Title: Police: Viral petrol station 'robbery' was a mix-up over identical cars
Article:
KEPALA BATAS: Police have classified a viral incident involving an elderly man accused of attempting to rob a motorist at a petrol station here as "no further action" (NFA).
Seberang Prai Utara deputy police chief Superintendent C. Tharmalingam said investigations revealed the incident at the Jalan Ahmad Badawi petrol station was a genuine mistake.
"The case has been classified as NFA because the man mistakenly opened the complainant's vehicle while stopping at the petrol station to refuel.
"Both the complainant's and the man's vehicles were of the exact same make and colour," he said in a brief statement today.
Earlier, a 40-second closed-circuit television (CCTV) clip circulated online showing a woman refuelling her car before an elderly man approached the vehicle.
The woman was seen fleeing the scene, while the driver inside the car sped off after noticing the man trying to open the vehicle's door, sparking widespread speculation on social media of an attempted robbery.
However, the elderly man's daughter, Facebook user Siti Nur Nadieya, clarified that her father had
mistaken the complainant's vehicle
for the red Perodua Alza multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) their family had rented for four days.
"My father has poor eyesight and did not check the vehicle's registration number at the time of the incident.
"He was supposed to refuel at pump number six, but went to a different pump by mistake. He also assumed the woman refuelling the car was a petrol station attendant.
"He then tried to unlock the vehicle using his remote key fob, and was puzzled when the doors failed to open. He only realised his mistake when the car sped off from the station," she said when contacted.
Siti Nur Nadieya's family was caught off guard by the viral allegations and had lodged a report at the Kepala Batas district police headquarters to clear the air.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar pays last respects to A. Samad Said
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was at the Saidina Abu Bakar As-Siddiq mosque in Bangsar here tonight to pay his last respects to National Laureate Datuk Seri Dr Abdul Samad Muhammad Said, better known as A. Samad Said.
The prime minister arrived at the mosque about 10.45pm and met with Samad's family to offer his condolences.
Anwar, together with the late writer's family members and mosque leaders, then recited the Yasin.
Earlier, Anwar and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, expressed their
sadness and sorrow
upon receiving news of Samad's death.
Samad
died at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL)
about 6.05pm. He was 91.
The news was confirmed by his second son, Helmy Abdul Samad, in a post on Threads.
Samad had been receiving treatment at HKL after being admitted yesterday evening due to age-related ailments, diabetes and a lung infection.

Title: Three arrested, six stolen vehicles seized in Kajang
Article:
KAJANG: Three people, including a woman, have been arrested and six stolen vehicles seized in an operation targeting a vehicle theft syndicate in Kajang, Serdang and Kuala Langat.
Kajang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the suspects, two men and a woman aged between their 20s and 30s, were arrested during Ops Lejang conducted by the district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Division between 3.45pm and 7.45pm yesterday.
He said the operation followed a police report lodged at 1.20am on Nov 22 over the theft of a Proton Iswara in Kajang Utama.
Police seized six vehicles between Nov 23 and 24: a Proton Iswara, Nissan Vanette, Proton Wira Aeroback, Mazda E2200 and two Toyota lorries.
"Initial investigations found that all 6 vehicles were linked to vehicle theft cases in Kajang and Serdang," he said.
Naazron said the suspects were also believed to be linked to other criminal cases in Kajang, Serdang and Kuala Langat.
He said all three had previous criminal and drug-related records and tested positive for methamphetamine in preliminary urine screening tests.
The suspects have been remanded for four days to assist investigations, while police are tracking down several others believed to be involved.
The case is being investigated under Section 379A of the Penal Code for motor vehicle theft and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Those with information can contact investigating officer Inspector Muhammad Nabil Aizat Rusdy at 013-6232713.

Title: NST Leader: Integrity must begin at the border
Article:
WHEN news broke recently that a Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) official had waved an undocumented female foreign national through Kuala Lumpur International Airport, readers could be forgiven for throwing up their hands in frustration.
Here is a newly minted agency  created specifically to keep our borders safe,  yet it is already staffed by   at least one individual who, if allegations are proven, is no better than  the Immigration Department personnel notorious for  leaving our borders so porous in the first place.
Redemption appears to have arrived almost as swiftly, with the revelation  that a female subordinate  was instrumental in securing  her superior's arrest by reporting his alleged misconduct.
Her action has rightly won the praise of her ultimate boss, MCBA director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.  "It only takes one person to change what is happening on the ground," he reportedly said of what the exemplary female officer did.
Shuhaily is right to come down swiftly — and hard, we must stress — on  any  errant officers within his ranks.
He must let it be known right from the get-go that he will brook no nonsense from his officers, regardless of rank, and that the  book will be thrown at anyone found guilty  of wrongdoing.
All MCBA staff must know that they work for an agency that has established, right from the start, a reputation for zero tolerance towards official misconduct.
The action of the female officer, with nary a thought for the possible fallout had her report against her superior backfired, deserves  praise not just from the higher-ups in her agency but from all Malaysians who believe that integrity in the public service still exists and is worth fighting for.
This singular selfless act mirrors another brave and creative move by Datuk Nor Salwani Muhammad from the Audit Department, who was instructed to leave  a meeting related to the 1Malaysia Development Bhd saga.
Ordered out of a meeting where she was supposed to take minutes, she discreetly left behind a digital voice recorder — capturing shocking discussions about tampering with the  audit report.
Enforcement agencies such as MCBA are on the front line of efforts — almost always a struggle even under the best of circumstances — to keep the government and the country  on the straight and narrow path. It has to be — and seen to be — scrupulously beyond reproach and imbued with unstinting integrity  to gain public trust  so critical to its long-term success.  Kudos to  female officers such as the one in MCBA.
Women may hold up half the sky, as the saying goes, and in this  instance, they have proven  that they are anything but the weaker sex.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi: A. Samad Said's literary legacy will continue to inspire Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: National Laureate Datuk Seri Dr A. Samad Said leaves behind an enduring literary legacy that will continue to inspire generations of Malaysians, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Fahmi said the late literary icon, commonly known as Pak Samad, had devoted his life to language and literature, not only through his writings but also by capturing the pulse of society, its struggles and the nation's journey through the eyes of a distinguished man of letters.
He said the late author's celebrated works, including Salina, Sungai Mengalir Lesu and Hujan Pagi, would remain an invaluable part of the nation's literary heritage and continue to be read and appreciated by generations to come.
"Although a literary figure may have departed physically, his voice, ideas and struggles will never be extinguished," he said in a Facebook post today.
Meanwhile, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said A. Samad's literary works had touched the lives of Malaysians by giving expression to emotions and sentiments that people might otherwise struggle to put into words.
"He helps us articulate feelings and messages that we may find difficult to express ourselves. Through his writings, we are invited to understand the lives of others and empathise with their hardships," she said in a Facebook post.
Fadhlina said she hoped the late writer's works and ideas would continue to be read and appreciated, particularly by the young generation, as they contain many valuable lessons for society.
Separately, Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching paid tribute to the late literary figure by quoting an excerpt from his poem, Hidup Bersama, which reflects his philosophy and lifelong struggles.
"Thank you for giving Malaysia its conscience and its poetry, Pak Samad. Your words will live on forever," she said.
A. Samad, whose birth name was Abdul Samad Muhammad Said, died at 6.10pm today at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) at the age of 91.
He had been admitted to the hospital due to age-related ailments, compounded by diabetes.
Born on April 9, 1935, in Kampung Belimbing Dalam, Durian Tunggal, Melaka, he was the fourth recipient of the National Laureate Award, which he received in 1985.
In recognition of his outstanding contributions to literature, he also received the Pejuang Sastera Award in 1976 and the SEA Write Award in 1979. -BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 12 of 29 MA63 issues resolved in four years, says Mustapha
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has resolved 12 of the 29 outstanding issues under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) over the past four years, marking its strongest progress in a decade, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.
He said the priority now was to ensure MA63 implementation remained a national agenda.
Among the developments were the gazetting of Sabah's interim special grant of RM1.5 billion annually, the launch of the MA63 Dashboard to allow the public to track progress, and discussions with the Election Commission on Sabah and Sarawak's representation in Parliament.
"The Madani Kenali Borneo Carnival, which began in Melaka, also provides an opportunity for more people to learn about the history of Malaysia's formation and the status of Sabah and Sarawak within the Federation," he said in a Facebook post tonight.
In conjunction with the fourth anniversary of the Madani Government, Mustapha thanked Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for giving him the opportunity to serve in three different portfolios.
"Starting as deputy human resources minister, then serving as deputy higher education minister and now as minister in the prime minister's department (Sabah and Sarawak), each responsibility has allowed me to hear people's needs first-hand and bring their concerns to the federal level," he said.
During his time at the Human Resources Ministry, he was involved in consultations on amendments to the Sabah Labour Ordinance, which provide workers with better protection, including 98 days of maternity leave, paternity leave for eligible employees and a 45-hour working week.
He said his tenure at the Higher Education Ministry focused on widening access to higher education for students from low-income families and strengthening students' rights.

Title: Three arrested over road rage assault of elderly man in Terengganu
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Police have arrested three men suspected of assaulting a 62-year-old man in a road rage incident in Lorong Ikhwan, Jalan Pasir Panjang, here yesterday afternoon.
Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred about 5pm after a Perodua Alza allegedly rear-ended a Skoda driven by a woman.
He said the woman's husband got out to inspect the damage but was allegedly punched, elbowed and kicked by the three men, sustaining injuries to his nose, mouth and face.
"He was taken to Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) for further treatment. Swift action by the Kuala Terengganu Criminal Investigation Department led to the arrest of the three suspects, aged between 39 and 44," he said in a statement today.
Khairi said the suspects would be brought to the Kuala Terengganu magistrate's court tomorrow morning for investigators to get a remand order to detain the three men to facilitate investigations under Section 325 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt.
Those found guilty under this section are liable to prison terms of up to seven years and a fine.
Khairi said police were continuing their investigations to establish the full circumstances of the incident, adding that they viewed road violence and aggressive behaviour seriously as such acts could threaten public order and endanger others.
A 20-second video went viral on social media yesterday showing a man in a black jacket and cap grabbing an elderly man's shoulder before
elbowing him
in the face by the roadside in rainy weather.

Title: Malaysia steps up focus on quantum technology, regenerative medicine
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is stepping up efforts to develop future technologies, including quantum technology and regenerative medicine, to strengthen its economic resilience amid global uncertainty and supply chain disruptions.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said strengthening the science, technology and innovation (STI) ecosystem was a key focus of the National Science Council's second meeting of 2026, which he chaired today.
He said the meeting discussed measures to improve Malaysia's ranking in the Global Innovation Index, develop the National Regenerative Medicine Biofoundry and advance the country's quantum technology capabilities.
The biofoundry project involves the Bioeconomy Development Corporation and Sarawak-based BioVerde Technologies Sdn Bhd.
"This strategic planning is crucial to ensuring that the country's STI capabilities are put to good use in addressing economic challenges, including financial uncertainty and global supply chain disruptions," he said in a post on X.
Anwar said each initiative would be closely monitored to ensure it remained on track and delivered tangible benefits.
The National Science Council serves as the highest-level platform for coordinating STI policies across ministries and agencies, in line with the National Science, Technology and Innovation Policy 2021-2030, which aims to transform Malaysia into a high-tech nation by 2030.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: Differences in political stance don't affect government administration
Article:
BALI: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi says differences in political views and positions among parties in the federal government do not affect the country's administration.
The Barisan Nasional chairman said political maturity enabled party leaders to set aside their differences when carrying out their shared responsibility of governing the country.
"When it comes to administering the government, we set aside those differences. When discussing matters concerning national interests, we remain highly professional, and there are no disagreements," he told Bernama.
He was responding to questions about the Parti Amanah 2026 National Convention held last Sunday, where delegates passed a motion, with the support of nearly all attendees, for the party to contest the 16th General Election (GE16) without cooperating with BN.
However, Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu was reported to have clarified that the resolution was merely a recommendation by the party to be submitted to the Pakatan Harapan presidential council, with any final decision on electoral cooperation to be made at the coalition level.
Zahid, who is also the rural and regional development minister, arrived in Bali on Monday for a five-day working visit to Indonesia, involving a series of official engagements on the resort island and in Jakarta.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'We come as twilight guests': A. Samad Said's son shares father's words of wisdom
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "Kita datang ini sebagai tetamu senja. Bila hujung nanti bawa dosa, bawa pahala" (We come as twilight guests. When the end arrives, we carry sins, we carry good deeds).
Those are lines from a poem written by the late National Laureate Datuk Seri Dr A. Samad Said, which stand among the meaningful messages his family hopes the public will remember.
The late writer's fourth child, Az Abdul Samad, 45, said that although his father did not have the chance to leave final words before breathing his last, the stanza reflected the principles and reminders he frequently shared during his lifetime.
"I hope the public can remember him through his works and the good things he did throughout his life," he said when met at the National Institute of Forensic Medicine (IPFN), Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL), here tonight.
Sharing his father's final moments, Az said he passed away peacefully, surrounded by close family members, grandchildren and friends, even though several of his other siblings live abroad.
Az said his late father, who suffered from health issues due to old age, would always be remembered as a very active individual who enjoyed walking, ate in moderation and often spent time in bookshops.
"He was always reading and sharing knowledge. Many people loved him, and I am very grateful to be his son. I ask everyone to continue praying for the well-being of the deceased's soul," he said.
Meanwhile, Az said funeral prayers would take place at 10am tomorrow at Masjid Saidina Abu Bakar As-Siddiq, Bangsar, before he is buried at the Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery.
Earlier, the late writer's second child, Helmy Abdul Samad, 63, said his father passed away at the age of 91 about 6.10pm at HKL.
A. Samad, whose real name is Abdul Samad Muhammad Said, was admitted to HKL yesterday afternoon due to old age and also suffered from diabetes. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia to set up joint working group to boost rural development
Article:
BALI: Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to establish a joint working group (JWG) to strengthen cooperation in rural development, including through the exchange of best practices in village management in both countries.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is currently on a working visit to Indonesia, said Malaysia could benefit from Indonesia's experience specifically its more structured village rating system to improve data collection and the effectiveness of rural development programme implementation.
He said Indonesia classifies its approximately 75,000 villages into four categories as developed, developing, lagging and severely lagging.
He added that this rating system could serve as a reference for developing an index or set of standards to measure the level of village development in Malaysia, which has about 15,000 villages.
This, he said, would assist the government in planning development programmes more effectively.
"We also aim to have an index or standard for ranking these villages something we have already implemented though their system is more structured.
"We can leverage this to further improve data collection and determine how such data can be utilised for the implementation of government programmes," he told Bernama during a visit to Tegallalang Village here today.
Zahid, who is rural and regional development minister, arrived in Bali yesterday for a five-day working visit to Indonesia, which includes a series of engagements on the resort island and in Jakarta.
He began today's agenda with a bilateral meeting with Indonesia's Deputy Villages and Development of Disadvantaged Regions Minister Ahmad Riza Patria in which both sides agreed to establish a JWG.
This was followed by the visit to Tegallalang Village and one to Mas Village.
Zahid said another approach worth studying was the Indonesian government's development of ecotourism, for instance, by transforming terraced padi fields as tourist attractions.
Doing so, he said, would see benefits shared not only by the farmers but by the entire village community.
He added that Indonesia also utilises village-owned enterprises known as "Badan Usaha Milik Desa" (BUMDes), which engage in economic activities such as the production of handicrafts for the export market.
He also cited rural development programmes such as "Desa Kirana" and "Desa Lestari" in Malaysia, as well as Indonesia's "Desa Mandiri" (Independent Village) programmes which are similar in nature but differ in implementation.
"By fostering this integration, they can learn from us, and we can learn from them, allowing us to further improve upon what has already been established," he said.
Zahid was scheduled to depart for Jakarta later today to attend the 14th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Management (AMMDM) and the 15th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Asean Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response (AADMER) in Tangerang, Banten.
Meanwhile, Riza said he plans to conduct a reciprocal visit to Malaysia in the near future to study the country's approach to village management and development.
"There is much we can learn specifically regarding the management of villages in Malaysia which will serve as a valuable experience for us," he said.
He also highlighted the need for both nations to collaborate on village development in the Malaysia-Indonesia border regions, not only to strengthen communication ties but also in terms of rural development policy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'He helped anyone in need': A. Samad Said remembered for generosity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Beyond his towering literary legacy, the late National Laureate Datuk Seri Dr A. Samad Said is remembered for his generosity in helping underprivileged youths pursue their education.
National Laureate Datuk Dr Zurinah Hassan said she was among those touched by his kindness, recalling how he agreed to act as guarantor for her Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) student loan when she studied at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM).
"When I was preparing to further my studies at university, I needed a guarantor for my MARA student loan. He did not hesitate to help me.
"Without his assistance, it would have been difficult for me to continue my education. He was incredibly helpful, not only in the field of writing but also in supporting my academic journey," she said during a Bernama Radio tribute programme at Wisma Bernama tonight.
Zurinah said his generosity extended to many others in need, regardless of their background.
"It was not just me whom he helped by becoming a guarantor; there were many others. That was simply his nature. He was an exceptionally generous person who would readily help anyone who approached him in need, regardless of their background.
"If someone came to Kuala Lumpur, he would even offer them a place to stay. He was always willing to help in whatever way he could," she said.
Reflecting on A. Samad's lifelong dedication to language and literature, Zurinah said he frequently reminded young writers to approach their craft with sincerity and appreciate human values.
She said his sincerity was reflected in his consistent efforts to champion ordinary people and marginalised communities through his works.
Zurinah urged younger writers to emulate his perseverance, noting that he produced major works despite limited resources, unlike today's writers who have access to modern technology and digital tools.
"Learn from the struggles of those who came before us. Today, we have many tools at our disposal, including laptops and smartphones, to support our creative work. Make the most of these opportunities to produce even better works," she said.
She said A. Samad's passing was a great loss to the nation, but was confident his lifelong efforts to elevate the Malay language, culture and literature would be carried forward by future generations. - BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Arthur: Asean's mineral wealth must benefit its people
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asean must ensure its mineral wealth benefits its people, drives innovation and protects the environment as global competition for critical minerals intensifies.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the region's mineral resources and growing economy had attracted global attention.
He said this presented Asean with an opportunity to shape how its resources were developed and ensure its people benefited from them.
"The world is looking to Asean, and for good reason. Our region is blessed with substantial mineral endowments and a dynamic, growing economy. But as we discussed, our ambition goes far beyond just extracting resources.
"Our true success will be measured by the value we create for our people, the innovation we spark in our industries and the care we show for our environment," he said.
He was speaking at the gala dinner for the 11th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Minerals and the Asean Minerals Investment Forum (AMVest) in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
The dinner also marked the fifth Asean Mineral Awards, which recognise achievements in mining, processing and distribution.
Arthur credited the engineers, geologists, technical specialists, management teams and host communities behind the nominated enterprises.
"These awards honour those who prove that commercial success and responsible business conduct are not mutually exclusive — they are mutually reinforcing," he said.
He also highlighted the importance of environmental protection, social responsibility and sound governance across the industry.
Earlier, at the ministerial meeting, Arthur said the global shift towards green energy and the growth of advanced industries had increased demand for secure and diverse mineral supplies.
This placed Asean in a strong position to generate greater value from its resources by processing them within the region.
"To achieve this, we must move beyond being a mere supplier of raw materials.
"We must pivot towards higher-value activities, including midstream mineral processing, advanced manufacturing, cutting-edge technological innovation and circularity," he said.
Asean has developed a common definition of critical minerals and identified a list of 30 minerals to guide investment.
Of these, 16 were identified from the perspective of producers and 14 from that of consumers. This gives the bloc a clearer picture of the resources it can supply and the materials its industries require.
The region is also exploring ways to recover and reuse minerals.
It is working with the United States on recovering materials from discarded electronics and with China on the sustainable use of rock aggregates, marine sand and other construction materials.
Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam are the first three countries to pilot the Investment-Ready Minerals Projects initiative.
The initiative aims to help project developers prepare proposals with sufficient information for banks and investors to assess their commercial viability.
Supported by the World Bank and the Asean Secretariat, the pilot projects will help shape a common set of guidelines and templates in 2027.
AMVest also provides developers with an opportunity to present their projects directly to potential financiers and connect with companies offering the technology they need.
At a joint press conference during the meeting, Arthur said Asean had launched Asean Minerals Connect, a digital platform that allows project developers to showcase their proposals to financiers across Southeast Asia.
The platform is expected to extend these opportunities beyond companies and investors attending the forum in Kuala Lumpur.
"Because while we want to embark on more projects in order to harness the value of the natural resources in our region, first we want to make sure that we do it in a sustainable and equitable manner.
"But in order to do that, our players also need access to financing," he said.
Asean deputy secretary-general for the Asean Economic Community Satvinder Singh said the platform would consolidate information from member states, allowing investors to compare opportunities across the region.
However, countries would retain control over the information they chose to publish.
"When investors want to invest in our region, they need reliable data, reliable information," he said.
He added that the platform was still in its early stages and would become more useful as member states contributed more detailed information.
Satvinder said the importance of bringing industry players and financiers together was evident at AMVest, where investors, mineral companies and technology providers were meeting and exploring business opportunities.
He said such engagement was among the objectives ministers had in mind when they established the forum.
On the impact of geopolitics on minerals investment, Singh said Asean welcomed both Chinese and Western companies.
He added that the region's willingness to work with a diverse range of partners had long helped it remain competitive in the global marketplace.
"We welcome all partners to come and work with us, and we are excited to see a variety of partners coming, engaging Asean.
"I think that has been Asean's strength, and that's what has made us relevant in the global marketplace."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump could gain up to US$15mil from Nvidia shares after Huang's return: FT
Article:
WASHINGTON: The spectacular rebound in Nvidia's share price following Jensen Huang's return as chief executive could have added as much as US$15 million to US President Donald Trump's holdings in the stock on Monday, according to calculations by the Financial Times.
Huang resigned on Nov 12 over extramarital affairs including one with a suspected Chinese spy, a departure that sent shares in the US chip giant tumbling.
News of his return sent Nvidia shares soaring more than 30 per cent and added more than US$900 billion to the company's market value.
According to the Financial Times, Trump may have owned as many as 370,000 shares in Nvidia as of Sept 30.
The newspaper based its estimate on the president's financial disclosures to the Office of Government Ethics, the most recent of which was filed on Nov 5.
The disclosures do not include precise figures for disposals and purchases of shares.
The maximum figure for his holdings was therefore calculated on the assumption of purchases at the upper limit of each range, and sales at the lower limit.
A report from ABC News, citing Trump's annual financial disclosure report, did not specify the number of shares he owned but said their value reached at least US$12 million by the end of 2025.
It added that his accounts have continued to trade Nvidia in recent months, citing separate filings.
Nvidia said Monday that it had reinstated Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the US government that he did not pose a national security risk.
Trump said Huang's return followed his own direct contacts with Nvidia's board.
"I've been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it," he told US broadcaster CNBC.
Ruben Gallego, a Democratic senator for Arizona, called for scrutiny of Trump's portfolio.
"We need to investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement," he said in a post on X. "This White House is the most corrupt in history."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RTM to broadcast special 'Dialog Negara' episode featuring Anwar tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Radio Televisyen Malaysia will broadcast a special episode of the high-impact national discourse programme, "Dialog Negara", featuring Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as the main guest at 9pm tomorrow.
The Broadcasting Department, in a statement today, announced that the 60-minute programme themed "Behind the Decisions" will be broadcast on TV1 and the RTMKlik app, as well as be simulcast on Bernama TV, TV3, Astro Awani, TV AlHijrah, and TVS.
According to the statement, the special episode opens up space for a deeper discussion regarding the considerations, challenges, and rationale behind major decisions made by the government in its efforts to strengthen national development and improve the people's well-being.
"Unlike conventional interview formats, this special 'Dialog Negara' adopts an open dialogue approach that brings together the prime minister alongside the host, a panel of experts from various industries and a studio audience.
"The discussion will focus on four main dimensions: Behind a Decision, Behind Reforms and Change, Behind the People's Hopes, and Behind Malaysia's Future," the statement said.
The department added that this approach allows viewers to understand not only the decisions implemented, but also the deliberation process, implementation challenges, and their impact on society.
Additionally, the programme will feature interactions with figures and representatives from various sectors — including economy, entrepreneurship, health, education, agriculture, governance and related fields — to enrich the perspectives of the discussion.
The department said organising the programme aligns with RTM's commitment as a public broadcaster to empower a mature, fact-based, and inclusive culture of discourse, while serving as a bridge between the people and policymakers.

Title: WTS Capital's Q2 profit rises 18pct on revenue surge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: WTS Capital Bhd, formerly known as Systech Bhd, posted an 18 per cent increase in net profit to RM1.48 million in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM1.25 million a year earlier, driven by higher revenue.
Revenue surged 188.5 per cent to RM48.03 million from RM16.64 million.
The growth was primarily driven by revenue recognition from its ongoing artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and computing solutions project, alongside higher contributions from other projects under its corporate solutions segment.
For the six months ended Sept 30, 2026, WTS Capital's net profit rose to RM2.93 million from RM734,000 a year earlier, while revenue surged 530 per cent to RM200.07 million from RM31.76 million.
WTS Capital said it will continue strengthening its project execution capabilities and expanding its range of solutions.
The company will also leverage its customer network and industry relationships to explore new business opportunities across the public and private sectors.

Title: Penang fast-tracks water projects as demand set to rise
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang is accelerating major water projects, including desalination and inter-state water supply, as demand is projected to rise by 27.2 per cent to 1,100 million litres per day (MLD) by 2032.
Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) chief executive officer Datuk K. Pathmanathan said demand stood at 865 MLD last year, with the projection based on feedback from the manufacturing sector, property developers and state development agencies.
He said Penang's limited land area and freshwater resources posed challenges to meeting future demand, particularly amid climate change.
"Penang occupies a land area of only 1,158 sq km. Looking ahead, we do not have sufficient in-state raw freshwater resources to support continuing rapid economic growth in the 2030s, let alone address the threat of climate change," he said in a statement.
The state's main raw water source, Sungai Muda, was also under pressure following increased water extraction by Kedah last year for its "5 Seasons in 2 Years Padi Cultivation Programme".
Pathmanathan said PBAPP had implemented several contingency measures since 2024 to protect consumers against disruptions to Sungai Muda and prevent the Air Itam and Teluk Bahang dams from running dry.
Under the Penang Water Supply Roadmap 2040, the Water Contingency Plan 2030 aims to increase treated water production by 602 MLD, build 4 water treatment plants in Seberang Perai and increase supply to the island.
The state also plans to purchase between 300 and 500 MLD of treated water from Perak under a project targeted for 2032, while exploring seawater desalination plants in the 2030s.
Pathmanathan said Penang's domestic water consumption averaged 267 litres per capita daily last year, 18.7 per cent above the national average.
He urged households to reduce usage to meet the state's target of 250 litres per capita daily this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: IGP: Tony Pua may be summoned over leaked Pardons Board meeting minutes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have not ruled out summoning DAP leader Tony Pua to assist in investigations into the disclosure of minutes from a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the matter would be referred to an investigating officer for further action.
However, he said police had yet to receive any formal reports concerning the issue.
"So far, no police reports have been lodged regarding the matter. It has only been circulated on social media and other platforms. Nevertheless, the police are prepared to investigate," he told reporters after the conferment of rank insignia to senior police officers.
Earlier, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail directed the police to
mobilise all available resources
to investigate the alleged disclosure of the meeting minutes.
This followed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's call for police to investigate the alleged leak and subsequent circulation of the document.
During Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar
denied allegations
that the government had released the confidential meeting minutes to the public.
He also dismissed claims that the document concerning Najib's conditional pardon had been leaked by the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department or the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
Instead, Anwar explained that certain portions of the document had been declassified by the A-GC to facilitate the preparation of responses in legal proceedings brought before the courts concerning the matter.

Title: No more ‘white, round pills’: MySejahtera’s second life as Malaysia’s digital health hub
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — What began as a mandatory crisis response tool at the height of the Covid-19 pandemic has evolved into the cornerstone of Malaysia’s national digital health infrastructure, serving as a digital front door for millions of residents.
Speaking to Malay Mail, Health Ministry Digital Health Division director Dr Maheshwara Rao Appannan said the MySejahtera application has successfully moved from contact tracing to a comprehensive public health platform, driving the ministry’s “One Person, One Record” vision.
From crisis tool to national platform
At the onset of the pandemic, the government identified a critical need for a digital tool to disseminate information and manage data. Adoption was massive, with nearly 32 million people onboarded.
Dr Maheshwara said inclusivity was key to the strategy.
“It was essential to include everyone residing in the country, not just citizens, because disease knows no boundaries or religion. We utilised that data to strategically identify the areas where vaccination was required most urgently,” he said.
He said Malaysia is now ranked first globally for digital pandemic management by Data.ai, a success that laid the foundation for turning the app into a national public health platform, which currently has between 12 and 15 million monthly active users.
No more “white, round pills”
Historically, patient information in Malaysia was fragmented, and patients moving between public and private facilities often struggled to recall their medical history or specific prescriptions.
Dr Maheshwara said patients frequently described their medication as “white, round pills” rather than by name, a gap the ministry is now closing through MySejahtera.
“Today, over 15 million individuals have their prescriptions and health records accessible within the application.
“With a single click, users can view lab results, dental history and radiological reports,” he said.
“We are empowering users by giving them their records at hand, allowing them to share that information with private practitioners, including both clinics and private hospitals,” he added.
Bridging public and private care
To support this ecosystem, the ministry set up the Malaysia Digital Health Certification Network.
The network currently connects more than 50 private hospitals and over 3,000 general practice clinics, allowing information to flow seamlessly between the public and private sectors while keeping care continuous.
Appointments: Public clinics first
MySejahtera is designed to be a digital front door that reduces the administrative friction often involved in navigating the national healthcare system.
Users can currently schedule appointments directly with public health clinics and dental facilities.
Dr Maheshwara said the booking function is focused on the public sector for now. While the app allows medical records to be shared securely between public and private facilities, appointments with private healthcare providers cannot yet be booked through it.
He said the ministry is actively working to expand these capabilities as part of a broader roadmap to make MySejahtera an all-in-one personal health management tool, allowing patients to manage their entire care journey, from booking to post-visit summaries, on their mobile devices.
Organ pledges go digital
Simplifying organ donor pledges was one of the top priorities in the app’s transformation.
Dr Maheshwara said the previous system relied on paper forms and physical cards, whereas pledges are now recorded in real time. Should a pledger pass away, physicians can immediately verify their donor status in the database.
The app also notifies the pledger’s nominee.
“When a user registers their organ donation pledge, that nominee receives a notification confirming the user’s decision. This is an important step, as it ensures that the next-of-kin is aware of their loved one’s wishes,” he explained.
Looking ahead, the roadmap includes integrating ambulance services into the app. The feature will automatically share a patient’s location during an emergency and link up with the 999 response system for faster, more accurate intervention.
Consent comes first
Addressing data security concerns, Dr Maheshwara stressed that health information is treated as sacred.
He said the platform runs on a consent-driven architecture to build digital trust, and access is never automatic.
There are two main ways to share records. With digital QR consent, users generate a secure, password-protected QR code containing only the information they choose to share with verified practitioners.
Under the explicit consent model, patients must manually approve a doctor’s request to view their historical records through the app, a process similar to approving a bank transfer.
The road to 2029
The ministry aims to fully digitalise all 2,918 primary care facilities and 670 dental facilities with electronic medical records by 2027.
All hospitals nationwide are slated to be fully digitalised by 2029, a longer timeline that reflects the more complex integration required in hospital settings.
Despite the technological leaps, Dr Maheshwara said the technology is merely a vehicle.
He said that in evolving from a pandemic tool into a lifelong health companion, MySejahtera aims to change how Malaysians manage their healthcare needs through their smartphones.

Title: Otters make a splash in KL’s Klang River, bringing hope for cleaner waters — and trouble for fish pond owners
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 24 — Beneath a tangle of highway in the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur, a family of otters rolls around in a patch of riverside sand, delighting the few passersby who notice them.
Small groups of otters are now being seen regularly in parts of the city, including along the once heavily polluted Klang River.
Theories vary on whether the smooth-coated otters, classed as vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, have returned to the city or were hiding in plain sight all along.
But their presence has raised hopes that efforts to clean up the Klang may be bearing fruit, and could inspire further improvement.
The Klang was once one of the world’s dirtiest waterways, designated a Class 5 severely polluted river under Malaysia’s rankings.
Years of work improved it to Class 3, or moderately polluted, which seems to have encouraged the otters to move in, said Malaysian wildlife ecologist Woo Chee Yoong.
“Wherever there are otters, there are fish. Wherever there are fish it means the whole river system... (is) clean, it’s healthy for all the communities around. So that’s one of the importance of otters,” he said.
In recent years, the animals have been filmed sunbathing on the river’s concrete banks and swimming in front of elevated metro stations, winning viral fame.
Retired soldier Hasan Ujang, who lives in a riverside apartment, enjoys watching their antics.
“We feel really happy when we watch them playing and playing, like kids swimming,” he said.
‘They have to survive’
But unlike otters in neighbouring Singapore, which are closely monitored by a network of citizen scientists, little is known about Kuala Lumpur’s otters.
Woo learned about them from local media reports on sightings in 2019 and the following year co-founded the Malaysian Otter Network (MON) conservation group.
“We don’t know how many groups are there, we don’t know how actually the otters are moving around,” he said.
Even the question of whether the otters have returned to the capital or were simply in less visible city environments before remains a “mystery.”
MON hopes to set up a citizen science system for people to report sightings.
Otters have been spotted elsewhere in the city, including at the Tropicana Golf & Country Resort, a high-end housing estate where they are less welcome visitors.
They are accused of raiding at least 12 houses in the past year. Their target: fish ponds.
Resident Yee Sze Mun, 89, said otters killed the beloved — and expensive — arowana fish he had nurtured for 15 years.
“They are a nuisance, but I can’t blame them, because they are just like us, they have to survive,” he said.
Residents say the incursions began last year after a company began clearing forest next door for a new development.
“We have an issue because they’re losing their habitat,” said residents’ association president Joy Appukuttan, who called the otter attacks a “grave concern.”
