Tropicana’s security team believes there are around 25 otters in the forest and the estate brought in Woo to teach residents how to deal with them.
The species is protected in Malaysia, so Woo urges residents to block entry points to their yards and install fences or netting over ponds.
‘An asset’
Datuk Seri Maimunah Mohd Sharif, a former Kuala Lumpur mayor and now advisor to the city on sustainable urbanisation, call the otters an “asset.”
“Otters are one of the benchmarks for clean cities,” she said.
Like others, she hopes a growing awareness of the Klang River otters can be harnessed to help improve the river further.
Hundreds of garbage traps were installed as part of the government’s River of Life project, and solar-powered “interceptors” deployed by a Dutch NGO have collected tens of thousands of tonnes of waste.
Now Maimunah wants to see more done to stop waste entering the river in the first place, and efforts to make the Klang Class 2B status, clean enough for body contact.
“One day, I want to swim in the Klang River,” she said.
Scarlett Koon Si Qi, a community architect and co-organiser of the annual Klang River Festival hopes the waterway can be restored to its natural banks without concrete lining.
“Some parts, maybe yes, you do need concrete to kind of protect and control for floods,” she said.
“But I think wherever we can, we should leave it as natural as possible.”
That would further benefit the otters, who need some vegetation and natural crevices to hide in, experts said.
The otters are already shifting views on the river, said Faith Foo, who runs the festival.
Growing up, “the teachers would always say that this is a very unsanitary place,” he said.
But seeing the otters, “it’s a reminder that that is a river.” — AFP

Title: Five minutes to Johor: Businesses hope new RTS Link with Singapore brings more than day-trippers
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 24 — If all goes according to plan, the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link will begin operations in February 2027, enhancing connectivity between Singapore and Malaysia, particularly Johor.
With a capacity to carry approximately 40,000 passengers daily and train frequencies of six minutes during off-peak hours and 3.6 minutes during peak periods, the light rail transit shuttle service connecting Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru and Woodlands North in Singapore is expected to generate economic opportunities across various sectors in Johor. The journey between the two stations is expected to take about five minutes.
From small traders to players in the transport and property industries, businesses are hopeful that the RTS Link will boost their earnings by bringing in more visitors from Singapore.
There is, however, another possibility: could the increased cross-border movement lead to Johor Bahru merely serving as a stopover, while the economic benefits are largely confined to businesses operating near the Bukit Chagar RTS station?
Small traders hope to reap benefits
Restaurant owner David Chiang, 65, believes the new rail service will attract more Singaporean customers, not only at weekends but also on weekdays, which are usually quieter.
“When the RTS starts operating, it will be easier for Singaporeans to come to Johor Bahru. They might come for breakfast or lunch, go shopping afterwards and then head straight home,” he told Bernama.
He said Singaporeans already make up a large proportion of the clientele at his restaurant at Jalan Trus here, which has been operating for about 80 years.
Murni Suratman, 51, who has been running a breakfast outlet in Tebrau since 2014, also sees a hike in visitors from Singapore, who generally have greater purchasing power, once the RTS Link is operational.
“It will benefit entrepreneurs, small traders and restaurant operators,” she said.
However, businesses located away from the city centre and popular tourist areas may not benefit to the same extent.
For instance, an asam pedas restaurant operator in Kampung Melayu here, who wished to be identified as Iena, expects visitors to favour established food destinations such as Senibong. Nevertheless, she hopes that upgrading the area surrounding her business premises would help attract new customers.
Traders interviewed by Bernama believe that the economic benefits of the RTS Link will not materialise automatically. Efforts will be needed to promote local products, highlight destinations beyond the established tourist hotspots and strengthen the competitiveness of local businesses.
Encourage overnight stays
While food operators are hoping for an increase in customers, the hospitality industry is endeavouring to turn short visits to Johor Bahru into overnight stays that generate greater visitor spending.
Malaysian Association of Hotels (MAH) Johor Chapter chairman Ivan Teoh said the RTS Link has the potential to benefit all segments of the hospitality industry, including five-star, mid-range and budget hotels, particularly those with convenient access to Bukit Chagar station.
He said hotel occupancy rates in Johor Bahru city centre currently stood at about 90 percent during weekends, with some hotels recording full occupancy during extended holiday periods.
The industry, therefore, expects the RTS Link to not only boost demand during peak periods but also stimulate bookings on weekdays.
“We expect occupancy rates to increase by between 20 and 25 percent during peak seasons,” Teoh said. “Smoother travel may encourage more Singaporeans to make day trips for shopping, dining and entertainment. However, Johor needs to offer more attractive experiences if it wants visitors to stay overnight.”
He believes healthcare and wellness services, medical tourism, diverse food offerings, entertainment and nature-based attractions could serve as additional draws, including for international tourists arriving via Singapore.
Destinations beyond Johor Bahru, such as Tanjung Piai, the various islands and nature-based tourism areas, could also encourage visitors to extend their holidays.
“Therefore, the main opportunity for the hospitality industry lies not merely in attracting more visitors, but in giving them more reasons to stay overnight,” he said.
Cannot sideline local entrepreneurs
Amid the potential growth in the tourism and service industries, questions have also been raised about the participation of local entrepreneurs in the business opportunities arising from the RTS Link development.
Johor Malay Economic Development Chamber president Zaini Atan said the organisation has proposed that at least 30 percent of commercial spaces within the RTS Link station area be allocated to local entrepreneurs, particularly Bumiputeras.
He said the station area is a good platform to introduce local brands to visitors from Singapore and international tourists, rather than being dominated by major business chains.
According to him, local coffee brands such as Kopi Tenggek and Kopi Teman Jiwa have the potential to be showcased as part of Johor’s identity.
“Our concern is that when the station opens, we may not see local companies represented there. Local businesses must be given the opportunity (to promote their products there). Otherwise, tourists may come without getting to see Johor’s own identity,” he said, stressing that all local entrepreneurs should be prioritised, regardless of race, provided that their products and businesses reflect their capabilities as well as the identity of the state.
Johor Malay Chamber of Commerce president Yazid Khalid identified the food and beverage, and retail and logistics sectors as among those likely to benefit directly from the RTS Link operations.
However, he said business opportunities should be offered transparently and announced well in advance to enable micro, small and medium enterprises to prepare in terms of financing, operational capacity and compliance with business requirements.
Yazid said an initial allocation of between 20 and 30 percent of commercial spaces for local businesses could be considered, alongside regular engagement sessions involving the state government, relevant agencies, project operators and business associations.
He added that the success of economic development should not be measured solely by investment value or an increase in visitor numbers, but also by the employment and business opportunities created for the local community.
E-hailing, property sectors
In the transport sector, the arrival of the RTS Link brings both expectations and challenges that need to be addressed in a balanced manner.
For e-hailing driver Mohd Sabran Md Sani, 47, the anticipated increase in passenger movement in Johor Bahru could boost demand for local transport services, but may not necessarily translate into better earnings for e-hailing drivers.
He said drivers were already under pressure from low fares, with some short trips generating net returns of as little as RM4, while they still had to bear fuel and vehicle maintenance costs.
He added that competition from bus services offering cheaper fares has also affected demand for e-hailing, particularly among Malaysians working in Singapore, who tend to prioritise lower commuting costs.
“There is no denying that the (RTS) project will have a major impact on the local transport industry. However, it remains uncertain how far the long-term benefits will extend as e-hailing drivers are currently grappling with various challenges, including fare rates that do not work in our favour,” he said.
Johor’s property market is also expected to benefit from the RTS Link as improved transport connectivity makes the state a more practical place to live.
Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association Malaysia (REHDA) Johor chairman Gerard Soosay, who is also chief executive officer of Sunway Property (Southern Region) and Sunway City Iskandar Puteri, said the combination of the RTS Link and the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) would serve as a key catalyst for the state’s long-term property market growth.
He said the approximately five-minute train journey between Bukit Chagar and Woodlands North could influence people’s decisions on where to live, work and invest.
“The RTS Link will make Johor more accessible, while the JS-SEZ will create more reasons for people to live and work here.
“It is the combination of these two factors that gives us confidence in the long-term prospects of Johor’s property market,” he said.
According to Gerard, Johor’s approved investments of approximately RM110 billion in 2025 and RM59.4 billion in the first half of 2026 also provide a positive foundation for the property sector’s growth when these investments translate into business openings and job creation.
He said the JS-SEZ is also expected to create at least 20,000 skilled jobs over the next five years, potentially stimulating housing demand among professionals and skilled workers.
Areas surrounding Bukit Chagar and the Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex and Johor Bahru city centre are expected to be among the first to benefit, while the development of a more comprehensive transport network could extend the impact to other areas.
However, Gerard cautioned that sustainable property market growth should not be assessed solely on expectations of rising prices but also be supported by actual transactions, rental demand and people’s decisions to settle in Johor.
“A sustainable property market is one where developers build responsibly, buyers make informed decisions and more Malaysians have the opportunity to own quality homes,” he said.
The views of economic players across various sectors suggest that the RTS Link has considerable potential to generate economic spillover benefits for Johor.
However, preparations for its operations should go beyond ensuring an efficient transport system to include strengthening the local economic ecosystem so that businesses and communities are well-positioned to capitalise on the opportunities ahead. — Bernama

Title: Teo: No licensing plan for online gaming firms as CMCF studies child safety risks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The government has no plans to introduce special licensing requirements for online gaming service providers, unlike those implemented for social media platforms, says Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching.
However, she said the Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) is conducting a study to assess emerging risks and appropriate regulatory approaches for online gaming services.
“The study covers child safety, user interactions, game features and content, as well as protective measures implemented by service providers.
“In addition, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is examining international practices as part of the assessment,” she said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates Motion for the Communications Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
She said the findings of the CMCF study will serve as the basis for determining whether additional protective measures or regulatory approaches suited to the Malaysian context are needed, taking into account industry developments, identified risks and the effectiveness of existing safeguards.
Teo said CMCF has held public consultations since September to develop a gaming subcode.
She said the consultations involve working groups comprising stakeholders such as operators, application and local and international game developers, online safety experts, the e-sports industry, legal practitioners and researchers.
“The feedback gathered through these public consultations will be considered to improve the subcode.
“Any need to review existing regulations will be assessed based on stakeholder feedback, current developments, identified risks and the effectiveness of the existing regulatory framework,” she said.
She said this approach ensures that regulations remain evidence-based and proportionate to risk, while prioritising user safety, particularly for children and teenagers.
Meanwhile, Teo said 202,402 items of fraudulent online content were taken down by service providers following requests from MCMC between Jan 1 and Nov 15.
On artificial intelligence company Anthropic’s claim that its technology was used in a political influence operation targeting users in Malaysia, Teo said the ministry is still awaiting further feedback from the company.
The Dewan Rakyat subsequently passed the 2027 operating and development expenditure estimates totalling RM2.613 billion allocated to the Communications Ministry under Budget 2027 by a voice vote, after 19 Members of Parliament debated the allocations.
The sitting resumes tomorrow.

Title: Even BN funded KLSCAH, Hannah Yeoh tells Parliament amid RM1,000 land premium row
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Barisan Nasional administrations had previously given public funds to the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH), Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said today, as she pushed back against claims of preferential treatment over a nominal RM1,000 land premium granted to the heritage building.
Speaking during a Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat this evening, Yeoh cited records showing that then Umno minister Tan Sri Rais Yatim had twice awarded conservation grants for the building.
KLSCAH received RM200,000 in 2005 and a RM500,000 conservation grant in 2007 under Rais, who was then Culture, Arts and Heritage Minister.
“From 2008 until now, for 18 years, they applied and did not receive anything. That is why they applied under the institutional category now,” Yeoh told the House.
“I hope after this there will no longer be issues played up outside claiming that this is a special case for KLSCAH.”
The DAP minister also sought to allay concerns over the status of Malay land in the federal capital, stressing that she had fought equally hard to preserve traditional Malay villages and Malay Reserve Land during her tenure.
Yeoh, who is Segambut MP, assured Parliament that the total size of Malay Reserve Land in Kuala Lumpur had remained unchanged at 2,477.375 acres since before she took over the Federal Territories portfolio.
“I give my guarantee that I will protect Malay Reserve Land,” she said, adding that Kampung Baru remains strictly governed under the Malay Agricultural Settlement (MAS) provisions, under which only Malays can reside there.
Yeoh said she had begun consultations with residents to formally zone traditional Malay enclaves, namely Kampung Sungai Penchala, Kampung Palimbayan and Kampung Bukit Lanjan, to preserve their heritage status.
She said it was an issue she had championed since her days as an Opposition MP for Segambut.
“I went into Parliament to defend Kampung Sungai Penchala. I said it must be retained as a traditional Malay village because everyone there is Malay, and you cannot find villages like this anymore,” she added.

Title: Replica of Picasso work recovered from 1MDB to feature at KL art fair this week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — A reproduction of a Pablo Picasso artwork linked to the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) case will be featured in a special exhibition space at the Malaysia Art Ecosystem Fair (MAEF) 2026, to be held at the Kuala Lumpur World Trade Centre from Nov 27 to 29.
National Art Gallery director-general Amerrudin Ahmad said the original work, titled L’Écuyère et Les Clowns, is a colour lithograph by Picasso dating back to 1961.
“The reproduction will be accompanied by information on the artwork’s background, artistic context, medium and visual interpretation as part of an art education approach for visitors.
“We see this interpretative approach as an opportunity to bring the public closer to artworks, not merely through visual observation but also by helping them understand their history, context and artistic value,” he told a press conference on MAEF 2026 here today.
Amerrudin said the exhibition space dedicated to the 1MDB-related artwork also aims to educate the public on integrity by highlighting the story behind the artwork.
However, Amerrudin said the original Picasso artwork, which was brought back to Malaysia in April this year along with three other artworks through 1MDB-related asset recovery efforts, would be displayed to the public at the National Art Gallery at a later date.
On the return of MAEF after a five-year hiatus, Amerrudin said its inaugural edition in 2021 brought together visual arts practitioners to discuss the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on the industry and formulate recovery measures.
“MAEF 2026 will place greater emphasis on boosting economic productivity, expanding markets and strengthening the competitiveness of Malaysia’s visual arts industry at the Asean and global levels.
“This shift in approach is important because we do not want the country’s visual arts industry to grow solely in terms of artistic production but also as an industry with a more professional economic structure and business network, and career opportunities,” he said.
MAEF 2026 will bring together 47 exhibitors, including art galleries, artist studios, museums, educational institutions and visual arts associations. The fair will also feature workshops and demonstrations, giving visitors an opportunity to witness the creative process behind artworks.
The exhibition is open to the public free of charge from 6 pm to 10 pm on Nov 27, and from 10 am to 10 pm on Nov 28 and 29. — Bernama

Title: Govt’s Duta Enclave valuation complied with law, Semantan Estate’s figure ‘excessively high’, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The High Court was told today that the Government’s valuation for acquiring 263.272 acres from Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd, known as the Duta Enclave, in 1956 complied with the Land Acquisition Act and Malaysian Valuation Standards.
Tan Tat Khuan, 40, assistant director of the Ministry of Finance’s Valuation and Property Services Department, testified that his valuation recommended compensation for land value only, unlike Semantan Estate’s claim, which covers both land value and compensation for severance and injurious affection (adverse effects from the acquisition).
“The plaintiff’s valuer assessed the land at RM1.5 million; my valuation is RM875,000. Why do I say the plaintiff’s valuation is inaccurate?
“Among the reasons is that he relied on comparable or land transaction evidence after the Dec 3, 1956 acquisition, which is not permitted by the First Schedule of the Land Acquisition Act.
“Furthermore, all the comparables by the plaintiff’s valuer were bungalow lots in Kenny Hill (now known as Bukit Tunku), whereas in this case the subject matter is a large tract of land with development potential.
“Other factors such as access and land use were also not taken into account in his valuation, resulting in an excessively high value,” he said.
Tan, the Government’s sole witness, was responding to a question from Justice Roslan Mat Nor at the hearing on the compensation assessment for the Duta Enclave today.
In earlier proceedings, Tan informed the court that in 1965, the Government of Malaysia paid RM1.39 million in compensation to Semantan Estate, higher than the RM875,000 he had recommended.
Justice Roslan also asked Tan whether the valuation submitted by the plaintiff conflicted with any established land valuation practice.
The witness replied that the plaintiff’s selection of comparable evidence contravened the Land Acquisition Act as well as a Federal Court decision on the method for valuing large tracts of land.
“In my rebuttal report, I explained that the selection of comparables contravened the Land Acquisition Act and a Federal Court decision holding that the valuation of large agricultural land cannot rely on bungalow plots as comparables.
“In a Johor case cited in my rebuttal report, the Federal Court ruled that residential plots cannot be used in the valuation of agricultural land,” he said.
At today’s proceedings, senior federal counsel Azza Azmi appeared for the Government, while counsel Ira Biswas appeared for Semantan Estate. The hearing resumes in March next year.
On Nov 13, 2025, the Federal Court dismissed Semantan Estate’s application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision that the Registrar of Titles for the Federal Territory need not register the 263.272-acre parcel in the Duta Enclave in the company’s name.
The Court of Appeal’s decision in the Government’s favour therefore stands, as the company cannot pursue its appeal to the Federal Court, and the case was remitted to the High Court for a hearing on compensation assessment.
On June 24, 2025, the Court of Appeal ruled that Semantan Estate is not entitled to ownership of the land, but is entitled to reasonable compensation based on the land’s value in 1956, when the Government took it over.
The land, in prime Jalan Duta, houses the Inland Revenue Board headquarters, several government buildings, the National Hockey Stadium, the Institute of Islamic Understanding Malaysia and the Federal Territory Mosque, among others.
In 2003, Semantan Estate filed suit against the Government alleging trespass arising from the unlawful acquisition of the land from the company.
In 2009, Judicial Commissioner Zura Yahya ruled that Semantan Estate retained its beneficial interest in the 263.27-acre parcel, which had been unlawfully acquired by the Government, and that the Government had trespassed on the land. — Bernama

Title: Nancy Shukri eyes homelessness Bill by 2028, says tackling foreign beggars needs inter-agency effort
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) aims to table a Bill specifically addressing homelessness by 2028 to tackle the issue more comprehensively and effectively.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the drafting of the proposed legislation was still at an early stage, with the ministry currently undertaking an in-depth study on the matter.
“God willing, perhaps in another two years or by 2028, we will have a Bill on homelessness to be tabled.
“We are just starting out, and are now conducting research on this matter,” she told reporters after attending a ministry gathering with media at Sultan Abdul Samad Building here today, with Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying and the ministry’s secretary-general Datuk Dr Maziah Che Yusoff in attendance.
Commenting further on the growing presence of foreign homeless people and beggars in the capital and across the country, Nancy stressed that the issue required inter-agency cooperation and was not the responsibility of any one ministry alone.
“When we conduct outreach operations, we work together with DBKL, the police and the Immigration Department to ensure that each agency and ministry addresses issues within its respective jurisdiction,” she said.
Nancy also expressed her appreciation to media practitioners, describing them as an important bridge in conveying the latest information on the ministry’s policies, services and new legislation to the public.
“Close cooperation between KPWKM and the media creates a win-win situation that not only helps the ministry but also greatly benefits society as a whole,” she said.
At the event, the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) received a Media Appreciation Award for its continued commitment to highlighting the voices of KPWKM’s target groups.
The award was presented by Nancy to Bernama News Service Executive Editor Mohd Haikal Mohd Isa.
The event also saw the symbolic handover of the KPWKM Campaign to Malaysian Women Journalists Association (PERTAMA) deputy president Nor Hasliza Abdullah, who is also Bernama’s English Language Editing Desk chief editor. — Bernama

Title: Anwar, Pakistan army chief Asim Munir discuss maritime security, counterterrorism cooperation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Malaysia and Pakistan are committed to strengthening defence and security cooperation, including through trilateral cooperation with Türkiye, while exploring opportunities for collaboration in maritime security and counterterrorism efforts.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in a Facebook post today that the matters were discussed during a courtesy call by Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir.
He said the meeting also provided an opportunity to exchange views on regional and international security developments, including efforts to ease tensions in West Asia and the importance of safeguarding global maritime security.
According to him, the discussions also touched on the need to prioritise dialogue and restraint in addressing border tensions while respecting national sovereignty and protecting civilians.
“This close cooperation is important in supporting peace, stability and mutual security, particularly in the region,” he said.
The Prime Minister also congratulated Syed Asim on his induction into the Hall of Fame of the Malaysian Armed Forces Staff College (MTAT). — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan Pakatan pledges loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz, says crisis must not derail 2027 state budget
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 23 — Negeri Sembilan Pakatan Harapan (NSPH) hopes for an immediate resolution to the prolonged political and administrative crisis in the state to ensure the smooth functioning of the government and safeguard the interests of the people.
In a statement today, the State PH Leadership Council said the crisis must be resolved in accordance with constitutional provisions, in line with the decree of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, to ensure continuity in the state administration and government institutions.
“Negeri Sembilan has been gripped by political and administrative uncertainty for more than 100 days. NSPH believes this situation has undermined the state administration’s priorities and raised concerns over the smooth running of government affairs.
“Negeri Sembilan should not continue to be a casualty of political manoeuvring by those entrusted with governing the state. The people gave them a mandate to work and address their problems, not to witness endless political bickering,” the statement read.
It said Negeri Sembilan did not belong to any political party, but was a state where the sovereignty of the Yang Dipertuan Besar’s institution must be respected, the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution upheld and the interests of the people prioritised.
NSPH also hoped the political disputes would not disrupt the upcoming State Legislative Assembly sitting and the tabling of the Negeri Sembilan 2027 Budget, as these would involve allocations for development, public welfare, infrastructure and the state’s economic continuity.
“Political disputes must not be allowed to leave the interests and future of the people of Negeri Sembilan neglected,” the statement said.
NSPH reiterated its allegiance to Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and its respect for the position and authority of the legitimate Institutions of the Four Undangs in their respective luaks, in accordance with customs, the law and the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution.
“This position is not driven by partisan political interests, but is rooted in the principle that the sovereignty of the Royal Institution, Constitutional Supremacy and State stability must be defended without compromise,” it said.
NSPH again called on all parties in Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional to cease their political disputes, respect the constitutional process and ensure that the state government resumes functioning in an orderly manner. — Bernama

Title: HRD Corp approves RM2.1b for worker training from this year’s levy collection, says deputy minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The Human Resources Development Corporation (HRD Corp) collected RM2.223 billion in levies this year, of which RM2.099 billion, or 94.4 per cent, was approved as financial assistance to fund training programmes for local workers.
Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the one per cent levy was imposed on employers with 10 or more local employees to fund human capital development, in accordance with the Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001 (Act 612).
He said HRD Corp used the levy collections to provide financing and training grants to employers to help improve workers’ skills through upskilling and reskilling programmes.
“The effectiveness of the levy is measured not only by the amount collected and utilised, but also by the impact of training on workers’ competencies, organisational productivity, workforce employability and industry needs.”
He said this when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 and the Development Expenditure Estimates 2027 at the committee stage for the Human Resources Ministry (KESUMA) in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Khairul Firdaus said HRD Corp also provided training grants in nine priority areas, including Industry 4.0, future technologies, fintech, blockchain and green technology, to ensure local workers remained relevant to current and future technological developments and industry requirements.
Meanwhile, he said records from the Department of Skills Development (JPK) showed that nearly 5,700 Orang Asli had participated in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programmes under the Malaysian Skills Certification System (SPKM) from 2021 to 2026.
The programmes covered areas such as Orang Asli community services, food preparation and automotive, in collaboration with training institutions including College Advanced Skills, Kolej Yayasan Pahang Advanced Skills and Yayasan Pendidikan MARA.
The government is also targeting 3,600 Orang Asli participants for skills training under the Mobile TVET initiative in 2027 to expand access, particularly in rural and remote areas.
He said KESUMA, through the Department of Manpower (JTM) campuses, was also expanding inclusive TVET training opportunities to all segments of society, including the Orang Asli community.
“The TVET programme also targets the Orang Asli community to improve access to and participation in skills training, and 168 Orang Asli have joined the programme as at Oct 31,” he said.
Khairul Firdaus said the employability rate of JTM TVET graduates stood at 98 per cent within six months of completing their training, while 85.4 per cent secured jobs related to their respective fields of training.
In another development, he said the Social Security Organisation (PERKESO) currently had 19 rehabilitation treatment panel centres throughout Sabah to provide recovery services for insured workers.
He added that PERKESO was open to exploring the phased implementation of satellite rehabilitation centres, depending on the suitability of locations.
The Dewan Rakyat subsequently approved KESUMA’s RM1.938 billion allocation for operating and development expenditure in 2027 by a majority voice vote, following a debate by 22 MPs. — Bernama

Title: MAHB moves to fix KLIA VIP room after Sabah minister slips, hurts head
Article:
SEPANG, Nov 23 — Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) has initiated immediate rectification action following an incident in which a guest slipped and sustained a head injury at the Terminal 1 VIP Room of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) earlier today.
In a statement today, the airport operator said KLIA regretted the incident and had addressed the feedback received from the affected guest.
“KLIA regrets the incident that occurred in the Terminal 1 VIP Room earlier today and has addressed the feedback received from the affected guest.
“The affected area has undergone a thorough inspection and necessary corrective measures have been fully implemented to ensure facility safety,” it said, adding that KLIA remains committed to maintaining a safe, secure, and comfortable environment for all airport users across all airport facilities.
Earlier, it was reported that Sabah’s Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Industry, Datuk Jamawi Jaafar, sustained a head injury requiring stitches after slipping in a restroom at KLIA this morning.
In a Facebook post today, Jamawi explained that the incident occurred due to a slippery floor surface while he was using a restroom near the Bunga Mawar Room in the KLIA VIP waiting area.
“In fact, a minor accident occurred while I was using the restroom near the Bunga Mawar Room in the KLIA VIP waiting area. The slippery surface caused me to slip, and my head struck the floor.
“Thanks to the doctor and nurse on duty at Menara Medical Clinics KLIA who treated and stitched up the wound earlier,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Kangar police nab two suspected cable thieves after chase, gang leader among five on the run
Article:
KANGAR, Nov 23 — Police have arrested two men believed to be members of the Mat Lan Keladi Gang, suspected of involvement in the theft of Telekom Malaysia ™ cables in front of Dataran Keris, Jalan Kangar-Alor Setar, here on Nov 17.
Kangar district police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the two men, aged 32 and 35, were arrested at 4.35 am following information from the public about a suspected cable theft at a petrol station in Taman Kemajuan here at 4.25 am.
He said that upon arriving at the petrol station, police found three cars, with seven men believed to be involved in the cable theft. They fled after noticing the presence of the police.
“Police pursued the suspects and managed to intercept a BMW carrying the two suspects, while the other two cars, a Volvo and a Volkswagen, believed to be carrying five other male suspects aged between 30 and 50, managed to escape,” he told a press conference at the Kangar District Police Headquarters here today.
Yusharifuddin said police believed the gang comprised the seven men, with the remaining five still at large and being tracked down, including the group’s leader. The gang was believed to have been active in cable theft over the past six months.
“Police also seized eight pieces of TM cables, each measuring approximately two metres, which had been cut, along with various tools used for cable theft. TM’s losses are estimated at RM4,000,” he said.
He said police believed they had solved nine cable theft cases recorded in the Kangar district between January and October following the arrest of the two suspects.
Yusharifuddin said the 32-year-old suspect had 33 previous criminal records, including narcotics offences, while the 35-year-old had three previous criminal records, also including narcotics offences.
He urged members of the public with any information on cable theft to come forward and provide information to the Kangar District Police Headquarters at 04-9082340 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: ‘Stay calm, have confidence’: PM Anwar’s message to SPM 2026 candidates
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today wished all candidates sitting for the 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination success.
In a Facebook post, he encouraged candidates to make the most of the hard work, sacrifices and preparations they had put in ahead of the examination.
“Stay calm, have confidence in your abilities and answer every question carefully. Continue to pray and seek the blessings of your parents and teachers.
“May everything go smoothly and may you be blessed with success, God willing,” he said.
A total of 420,879 candidates have registered for the 2026 SPM examination at 3,334 examination centres nationwide, with the written papers scheduled from Nov 23 to Dec 17. — Bernama

Title: Zahid to attend Huffaz 26K 2026 gathering as 27 tahfiz institutions set for recognition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The Huffaz 26K 2026 gathering in Bagan Datuk, Perak, this Friday is expected to strengthen cooperation among tahfiz institutions and expand education and career opportunities for Quran memorisers.
The Deputy Prime Minister’s Office said in a statement today that the gathering would bring together religious, academic and skills training institutions to strengthen the country’s tahfiz education ecosystem.
“The gathering reflects the government’s continued commitment to upholding the Quran, strengthening tahfiz institutions and empowering huffaz as important assets in the nation’s human capital development,” it said.
Themed “Huffaz Memacu Peradaban” (Huffaz Driving Civilisation), the gathering will also focus on expanding technical and vocational education and training (TVET) pathways for tahfiz students.
The theme reflects a shift in the development of tahfiz education, aimed at producing not only Quran memorisers but also scholars, educators, technocrats, professionals and leaders capable of contributing to national progress.
A total of 27 tahfiz institutions that have passed quality assessments conducted by the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM) are expected to receive recognition at the gathering.
Special awards will also be presented to 10 outstanding tahfiz institutions based on their performance and quality assessments under the Malaysia Tahfiz Recognition Standard (SPTM), while 20 SPTM assessors will receive certificates of appreciation.
The recognition follows a RM500,000 incentive announced by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi at last year’s gathering, with each selected institution receiving RM50,000.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, is scheduled to attend the gathering at Masjid Tuminah Hamidi, which will bring together Quran memorisers, tahfiz institution heads, religious teachers, educators and representatives of tahfiz institutions nationwide.
“Between 2023 and 2025, a total of 2,364 tahfiz students enrolled in skills training programmes at TVET institutions,” the statement said.
The statement said the government would continue strengthening the implementation of the National Tahfiz Education Policy and SPTM to ensure tahfiz institutions meet the required standards in education, governance and management.
The gathering is led by the Deputy Prime Minister’s Office in collaboration with JAKIM, PERMATA Al-Quran, Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA), Yayasan Pahang, the National TVET Council Secretariat and other relevant agencies.
Among the activities lined up are the TVET-Tahfiz Exploration programme, Interactive Quran Clinic and sharing of best practices among tahfiz institutions, alongside the Bagan Datuk Bermunajat programme involving the local community.
The programme will begin on Thursday with artefact exhibitions, agency booths and Quranic educational activities, before culminating in the main gathering on Friday. — Bernama

Title: No app, no personal data — Fahmi says MySiren alerts go straight to phones
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The National Early Warning System (MySiren), launched today, will function only by sending notifications to users, without having access to any personal data belonging to device owners.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the system, operated by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), uses Cell Broadcast System (CBS) technology to deliver alerts directly to compatible mobile phones within designated geographical areas, without requiring users to install an application or register.
“MySiren is different from the SMS (short messaging service) method, whereby messages are sent to recipients’ phone numbers. The system being used does not retrieve any information or data from users’ devices.
“It also does not incur any cost to message recipients,” he said at a press conference after launching MySiren at the Parliament building here today, which was also attended by Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching and MCMC chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din.
Fahmi said a nationwide simultaneous test of MySiren’s alert reception system is scheduled for 10.10 am on Nov 29.
Elaborating on MySiren, Fahmi said the system can deliver information or alerts to all devices much faster and simultaneously compared with the SMS delivery method.
“With SMS, messages have to go through a queue managed by telecommunications companies. This system bypasses the telcos and goes straight to what we call transmitters, with all telecommunication towers able to function as transmitters for disaster warning messages.
“So, all users within the coverage area of an active telecommunication tower or transmitter will receive the same information at the same time,” he said.
Fahmi said the MCMC would remain responsible for operating the MySiren system, while authorities such as the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) and local authorities (PBT) would also be able to access the system.
“At present, the focus is on notifications for floods, landslides and natural disasters, but this will be expanded to cover other information, including fires, missing persons or children, as well as disaster-related matters involving local authorities,” he said.
According to Fahmi, MySiren began development in 2025 after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the initiative during the tabling of Budget 2025 in October 2024, with a total cost of RM200 million.
Meanwhile, the MCMC said in a statement that it also conducted a system simulation at the Parliament building today to test its ability to send messages accompanied by alert sounds directly to compatible mobile phones within designated areas.
For the nationwide simultaneous MySiren alert reception test on Nov 29, the public is advised to update their mobile phones to the latest operating system versions or at least iOS 27.2 for iPhones, Android 12 for Android phones and EMUI 16 for Huawei phones.
“Users should also ensure that emergency alert settings, such as Government Alerts or Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA), are activated on their respective devices.
“Alert reception is subject to device compatibility, phone settings, as well as the coverage and availability of 4G or 5G mobile networks,” it added.
The MCMC said it would continue working with NADMA, relevant technical agencies and telecommunication service providers to ensure the system is ready for operation before expanding its implementation.
The public can find more information about MySiren at www.mcmc.gov.my/mysiren and through MCMC’s official social media channels. — Bernama

Title: ‘Purpose not fulfilled’: Wong Soon Koh and grandson quit PDP, vow loyalty to GPS
Article:
SIBU, Nov 23 — Bawang Assan incumbent assemblyman Datuk Seri Wong Soon Koh and his grandson Sean Wong have resigned from the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP).
Wong, who was PDP senior vice-president, formally tendered his resignation yesterday, giving up all party positions and appointments with immediate effect.
His grandson, a Sibu Municipal Council councillor, has done the same.
Wong said that after careful consideration, he had concluded the party’s current political direction no longer reflected the purpose and expectations behind his decision to join it.
“The original purpose of joining PDP has not been fulfilled. I don’t want to dwell on it because that will bring ill feelings from some other party,” he told a press conference here today.
On April 6, 2024, PDP president Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing announced that Wong and two senior leaders of the now-dissolved Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) have taken up top positions in PDP.
Meanwhile, Wong, who has represented Bawang Assan for about 35 years, indicated he is willing to make way for younger leaders in the coming state election.
He stressed that leaving PDP did not mean withdrawing support for Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) or Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
Asked whether he would join another party, Wong said he had not decided, but would only consider joining a GPS component party as an ordinary member, without seeking any leadership post.
He also pledged to back whoever GPS nominates for Bawang Assan.
Wong added that he had not discussed the matter with Engkilili state seat incumbent Dr Johnichal Rayong Ngipa, who separately announced his resignation from PDP today. — Bernama

Title: Melaka govt accepts Khoo’s apology over Terengganu Friday closure remarks
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 23 — Muslim male workers in Melaka whose employers bar them from attending Friday prayers have been urged to report the matter to the authorities immediately so that action can be taken against those involved.
State Religious Affairs, Entrepreneur Development, Cooperatives and Cost of Living Committee chairman Datuk Rais Yasin said preventing Muslim men from attending Friday prayers was inappropriate, as the prayers were an obligation for all Muslim men who had reached puberty, in Malaysia and abroad.
“Employers in Melaka and across the country should be aware of this, especially in a society as diverse in terms of race and religion as Malaysia.
“Alhamdulillah, we have yet to receive any reports of such incidents involving retail outlets, factories or other business premises in the state. Nevertheless, anyone facing such a situation should report it immediately to enable the necessary action to be taken,” he told reporters at a press conference here today.
He was responding to a question on whether Melaka would consider temporarily closing business premises to allow Muslim employees to attend Friday prayers, following a similar practice in Terengganu.
In a Facebook post, Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong expressed concern over a directive in Terengganu requiring business premises to close for two hours every Friday, between 12.30 pm and 2.30 pm.
Rais said the Melaka state government saw no need to adopt the proposal for now, adding that the situation in the state remained peaceful and harmonious.
“However, if he (Khoo) wishes to see the measure introduced, he can certainly propose it. His comments have also sparked discussion about its implementation, particularly on social media,” he said.
He also cautioned political leaders against politicising sensitive issues, especially those concerning religion, race and the royal institution (3Rs), warning that doing so could fuel misunderstandings and disrupt harmony in Malaysia’s multiracial society.
“The state government has accepted Khoo’s apology for his remarks about the temporary closure of business premises in Terengganu during Friday prayers and for drawing Melaka into the issue.
“The state government does not intend to file a police report over his remarks for now, as it hopes to resolve the matter amicably,” he said. — Bernama

Title: EC gazettes October electoral roll with 41,958 new voters, opens inspection until Jan 21
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 23 — A total of 41,958 Malaysians aged 18 and above were automatically registered as new voters in October, according to the Election Commission (EC).
EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the registrations were included in the October 2026 Supplementary Electoral Roll (DPT BLN10/2026), which was gazetted today and is open for inspection for 60 days until Jan 21, 2027.
He said the supplementary roll also recorded 17,076 registered voters who had changed their electoral constituencies and 4,109 who had changed their voter category or status.
“The EC urges Malaysians who turned 18 between Oct 1 and 31, 2026, as well as registered voters who have applied to change their electoral constituencies or voter category or status, to check their names in the DPT BLN10/2026,” he said in a statement here today.
He said individuals who found that their names were missing from the roll could submit claims by completing Form C through the MySPR online application or by visiting the relevant State Election Office.
Khairul Shahril said registered voters who wished to object to the inclusion of voters who had transferred into their electoral constituencies could submit their objections using Form D.
He said the EC had provided four channels for checking the supplementary roll: its official portal at www.spr.gov.my or mysprsemak.spr.gov.my, the MySPR online application at myspr.spr.gov.my, the MySPR Semak mobile application, and the hotline at 03-8892 7218.
He said claim and objection forms could also be downloaded from the EC portal before being submitted to the relevant State Election Director, together with the prescribed objection fee, during office hours on any working day throughout the inspection period.
For further enquiries on the DPT BLN10/2026 inspection process, the public can visit the EC’s official portal at https://www.spr.gov.my, call 03-8892 7218 or contact any State Election Office. — Bernama

Title: Rubber tapper finds missing toddler safe after overnight search in Kuala Krai
Article:
KUALA KRAI, Nov 23 — The parents of a 20-month-old boy who was found safe this morning after going missing since Sunday afternoon broke down in tears of relief and gratitude, thanking Malaysians for their prayers and support throughout the search.
According to Sinar Harian (SH), Muhammad Irsyad Hakim Mohammad Khairul Najmi was found at about 10.20am in a hilly rubber plantation near Kampung Bechah Salak here.
His father, Mohammad Khairul Najmi Mohd Rosli, 26, said he had barely slept since learning of his son’s disappearance, having rushed back from Bandar Jengka, Pahang, and joined the search effort through the night.
“Since yesterday, I’ve been searching for my son and haven’t been able to sleep. Alhamdulillah, a rubber tapper found him safe.
“We are so relieved. It is through everyone’s prayers that our son was found,” he told SH at the family’s home, visibly emotional.
Mohammad Khairul Najmi, a lorry driver, said his son was taken to hospital for precautionary checks following his ordeal in the forested rubber plantation.
The family reside in Bandar Jengka, Pahang, but had travelled to Kampung Bechah Salak, Nur Fatihah’s hometown, for a week-long visit.
Nur Fatihah, 24, said she had arrived at the village at about 1pm on Sunday after a nine-hour drive. Tired from the journey, she bathed Muhammad Irsyad Hakim before letting him play in the yard with his 16-year-old aunt while she took a rest, SH reported.
When she woke up, the toddler was nowhere to be found, she said, adding that the teenager had also dozed off. The family later found only the child’s pacifier outside the house and were unable to locate him despite searching the surrounding area.
“He’s still not able to speak properly and only says ‘mama’ and ‘papa’. He’s not familiar with this area and would usually become frightened and cry if he wandered too far from us.
“I don’t know how he managed to go so far this time, but thankfully he was found safe,” she said.
Nur Fatihah said the family was immensely grateful that the youngest of their two children had been found alive after an anxious search that drew widespread public attention and support.

Title: Rumours of early Perak polls? Saarani says government still has a year
Article:
IPOH, Nov 23 — Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said there are no plans or need to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly immediately after the tabling of the state’s Budget 2027 tomorrow.
He said the decision to dissolve the state assembly falls under the prerogative powers of the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, and that reasonable grounds must be provided before submitting any request for dissolution.
“The state administration still has about another year to fulfil the mandate given by the people and focus fully on the state’s development,” he added.
He told reporters this after attending the eighth edition of the Perak State Government Meet The Clients Day (HBP) MESRA Programme at Stadium Indera Mulia here today.
On Nov 18, the Perak Menteri Besar’s Office dismissed claims circulating on several social media platforms that Saarani had an audience with Sultan Nazrin Shah to seek, and had obtained, the Ruler’s consent to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly.
Meanwhile, Saarani said cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perak Pakatan Harapan (PH) remained strong and unaffected despite the two coalitions having contested against each other in several previous state elections. — Bernama

Title: Govt screens foreign workers with police checks, targets lower migrant workforce by 2030
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — The government conducts background screenings of foreign workers through an integrated system with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to ensure they have no criminal records before being allowed into the country.
Human Resources (Kesuma) Deputy Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said the measure is part of the screening mechanism to prevent unwanted incidents in the country.
“We are well aware of the various incidents that have occurred recently. Any foreign worker seeking employment must undergo the stipulated processes, which must be adhered to by employers intending to hire foreign workers.
“Therefore, we will continue to explore the best approaches to reduce the incidents mentioned earlier and to safeguard the safety of our fellow citizens,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Nurul Amin Hamid (PN-Padang Terap) on the government’s measures to ensure foreign workers are made aware of Malaysia’s laws and safety concerns, which was prompted by incidents such as a policeman’s hand being severed in a machete attack and a 15-year-old teenager being assaulted by a foreign national.
Meanwhile, in response to William Leong Jee Keen’s (PH-Selayang) original question on measures to reduce reliance on foreign workers, he said the government has set a target to reduce the ratio of Temporary Employment Visit Pass (PLKS) holders from 13 per cent in 2026 to 10 per cent in 2030.
He said the foreign worker intake ceiling is expected to drop from 2.248 million in 2026 to 1.788 million in 2030, in line with the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).
As of Oct 15 last year, he said, 2.082 million foreign workers holding PLKS were recorded in the Immigration Department’s system, MyIMMs, while the remaining national quota ceiling for 2026 stands at 241,178.
He said the government has also abolished the sectoral percentage calculation for foreign worker hiring quotas and will instead use the annual hiring ceiling projections set out in 13MP.
On efforts to prioritise local workers, he said employers must advertise vacancies on the MYFutureJobs portal for at least 14 working days and obtain prior approval under Section 60K of the Employment Act 1955 before applying for a foreign worker quota.
The government is also encouraging the use of technology, automation and mechanisation, as well as upskilling and reskilling programmes through HRD Corp, the Social Security Organisation (Socso) and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions to reduce reliance on foreign workers. — Bernama

Title: After KLIA fall, Sabah minister urges better toilet safety and emergency access
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Sabah Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Industry Minister Datuk Jamawi Jaafar required stitches to his head after slipping on a toilet floor at the VIP lounge in the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) this morning.
In a Facebook post, Jamawi said the incident occurred while he was using a toilet near Bilik Bunga Mawar in the airport’s VIP waiting area.
“Actually, it was a minor accident while I was using the toilet near Bilik Bunga Mawar in the KLIA VIP waiting area.
“The slippery toilet floor caused me to slip and my head hit the floor,” he said.
Jamawi said several acquaintances who bumped into him at the airport while his head was wrapped in a bloodied towel later contacted him to ask what had happened.
He also expressed his appreciation to the doctors and nurses at Menara Medical Clinics KLIA for providing treatment and stitching the wound on his head.
Following the incident, Jamawi urged Malaysia Airports to improve safety conditions in airport toilets and ensure emergency access routes to the nearest clinic were available.
He also said airport personnel should be given proper training to ensure they could provide immediate emergency assistance when needed.
The Melalap assemblyman was scheduled to continue his journey back to Kota Kinabalu at 1.05pm after completing a working visit to Brasília, Brazil.

Title: ‘Why did he run away?’ Father of woman killed in Federal Highway crash demands answers
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 23 — The father of a 20-year-old woman killed in a Federal Highway crash has questioned why the Mercedes-Benz driver, who is still being sought by police, allegedly abandoned the scene instead of facing the consequences.
The crash claimed the life of Tan Si Yin and another female passenger after both were thrown from the vehicle.
“Why did he run away and leave my daughter behind after the accident? If he was at fault, he should have taken responsibility,” Tan’s father told Berita Harian (BH) during her funeral today.
Speaking to reporters, the grieving father, who declined to be named, struggled to contain his emotions as he expressed disappointment over the driver’s alleged decision to flee rather than cooperate with investigators.
The family, however, said they did not wish to comment further and would leave the matter to the police.
According to BH, a sombre atmosphere hung over the Kwong Tong Memorial Centre this morning as around 20 relatives and close family members gathered from as early as 8am to pay their final respects.
At about 9.25am, the hearse carrying Tan’s body left for the Cheras Crematorium, accompanied by family members for the cremation.
It was reported earlier that the fatal crash occurred at about 5am on November 21 at Kilometre 34 of the Federal Highway heading towards Kuala Lumpur.
Police said a gold-coloured Mercedes-Benz is believed to have lost control before crashing into an embankment on the left side of the highway and spinning.
The impact threw Tan and another female passenger, who were seated in the rear of the vehicle, out through the back windscreen. Both were pronounced dead at the scene, while the driver allegedly fled.
Police are continuing efforts to trace the driver, and the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: Cash offers and sponsored holidays: PAC flags ‘serious’ governance failures in UKM’s outsourced postgraduate programmes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia’s (UKM) previous administration sat on conflict-of-interest allegations for nearly eight months, while legal officers were said to have been offered cash and holiday sponsorships to fast-track contract reviews, Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC) revealed today.
The findings were detailed in a damning report tabled in the Dewan Rakyat following proceedings into financial governance lapses at UKM’s Centre for Shaping Advanced and Professional Education (UKMShape), which the bipartisan committee described as “serious governance failures”.
PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the committee’s investigation, triggered by the Auditor-General’s Report 1/2026, found that complaints over conflicts of interest were left unaddressed until the university’s new leadership stepped in and launched an internal probe.
“There were also revelations that UKM’s Legal Advisory Office (PUU) faced continuous pressure, including offers of cash as well as sponsored overseas holidays to work on weekends in order to jump the queue for legal reviews on contracts,” Mas Ermieyati told a press conference in Parliament.
The PAC also said it found attempts to conceal the names of officers holding key positions in Koperasi Siswazah Bangi Berhad (KSBB).
According to its website, the cooperative acts as a third-party education facilitator and strategic partner, primarily recruiting and managing students for UKM’s postgraduate programmes, namely the Master of Education and the Postgraduate Diploma in Education.
Under the disputed agreements with UKMShape that date back to 2017, KSBB was contracted to handle student administration, logistics, and learning management support, but was found to have collected tuition fees directly from enrolled students before remitting a share to the university.
The dispute has since spilled into the courts, with the cooperative filing a civil suit at the Shah Alam High Court on May 4 seeking RM2.496 million. This prompted UKM to file a counterclaim for RM3.44 million in fee arrears alongside third-party notices against the former UKMShape director and former KSBB chairman.
Mas Ermieyati, MP for Masjid Tanah, said the PAC’s investigation found that even UKM’s Internal Investigation Committee (JKSD) initially suffered from structural conflicts of interest.
Panel members were appointed directly by the vice-chancellor and the inquiry’s scope was restricted to junior staff rather than top decision-makers, including the former vice-chancellor. The JKSD has since widened its probe to call in the relevant senior officials.
The PAC is now recommending 10 sweeping reforms that it said would help restore financial integrity across public universities, including urging the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission to investigate and prosecute those behind the cash and holiday offers to UKM legal officers.
It is also urging a ban on third-party entities collecting student fees and called on future independent inquiry panels to be appointed directly by the university’s board or the Higher Education Ministry rather than the vice-chancellor.

Title: Selangor sets aside RM3m for free meals for 73,594 SPM candidates
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 23 — The Selangor government has allocated RM3 million to provide free meals to 73,594 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) candidates across the state under the Selangor Nutrition (NutriSel) SPM 2026 initiative.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the special initiative, funded through allocations from the State Economic Planning Unit (UPEN) and Menteri Besar Selangor (Incorporated) (MBI), aims to provide nutritious meals to support students’ needs, concentration and well-being throughout the public examination period.
He said a total of 71,152 SPM candidates from 256 schools would benefit from the initiative, covering Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK), Sekolah Agama Menengah (SAM), Sekolah Agama Menengah Tinggi (SAMT), Sekolah Menengah Persendirian Cina (SMPC), special model schools and private tahfiz schools.
“Another 2,442 SPM candidates from 20 schools or institutions will also benefit. These include full boarding schools (SBP), integrated full boarding schools (SBPI), Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama (SMKA), Maahad Integrasi Tahfiz Selangor (MITS), MARA Junior Science Colleges (MRSM) and special education institutions.
“All the students will receive free meals over the five days of examinations for core subjects, with distribution coordinated by UPEN, the Selangor Education Department (JPN) and the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais),” he said after the symbolic handover ceremony for the NutriSel 2026 at MTIS Alam Impian here this morning.
Also present were deputy state secretary (Development) and UPEN director Datuk Johary Anuar, Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad, and MBI chief executive officer Datuk Saipolyazan M Yusop.
Under NutriSel SPM 2026, candidates at the 256 schools will receive nutritious lunch sets worth RM8 per day, while those at the 20 schools or institutions will receive food baskets containing vitamin C tablets, bread, cereal and milk.
Amirudin, who is also the Selangor Education and Human Capital Development Committee chairman, said the initiative was in line with the state government’s commitment to safeguarding students’ welfare and well-being, particularly as they sit for their examinations.
“We are focusing on providing strong support to ensure students excel and helping them obtain nutritious food before their learning sessions.
“This also supports the people's welfare agenda and efforts to develop quality human capital in Selangor in the future,” he said.
Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state Education Department would continue to monitor the situation of SPM candidates affected by floods who were still taking shelter at temporary evacuation centres (PPS) in the state.
“During my previous visits to the PPS, I came across several affected students, and we will address related matters, including transportation arrangements.
“The flood situation has improved so far, and we will look into assisting with the clean-up of flood victims' homes,” he said.
Earlier, Amirudin handed over food baskets to 50 SPM candidates at MITS Alam Impian, as well as RM50,000 in assistance to upgrade the school’s musolla and sports facilities. — Bernama

Title: Johor sets aside RM5m to spruce up Larkin Sentral by Christmas after MB’s surprise visit
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 23 — The Johor government has allocated RM5 million for maintenance and improvement works on facilities at the Larkin Sentral Public Transport Terminal in Johor Bahru.
State Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said the works will be carried out in phases as a short-term effort to upgrade the facilities.
He said the works, which do not involve high costs or large-scale infrastructure upgrades, are expected to be completed by December 25.
“The identified repair works include the maintenance of infrastructure and public amenities, as well as improvements to cleanliness and passenger comfort.
“This is in addition to repair works by the Larkin Sentral operator on automatic doors B and C, the emergency exits and the roller shutters at the retail area,” he told reporters at the Johor state legislative assembly sitting in Kota Iskandar here today.
Mohamad Fazli said cleanliness and user comfort are top priorities, particularly the condition of restrooms throughout the terminal, including those on the ground floor and on the first floor near the tailor shops.
“Basic supplies such as tissue paper and soap must always be sufficiently stocked, and the management is required to submit weekly reports on the status of the restrooms,” he said.
He added that the restrooms must be kept clean and comfortable for users.
Mohamad Fazli, who is also the Bukit Pasir assemblyman, said the terminal’s management has been issued a warning to take immediate action on the maintenance shortcomings identified and to ensure the problems do not recur.
He stressed that the building being more than 30 years old should not be used as an excuse to neglect maintenance, especially since the terminal is one of the main gateways into Johor Bahru.
“The state government has set a timeline to ensure the repair works are carried out accordingly,” he said.
Johor Mentri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi recently made a surprise visit to Larkin Sentral, where he reprimanded the management over dilapidated facilities, unsanitary restrooms and years of neglected maintenance.
In a video shared on social media, Onn Hafiz was seen reprimanding those responsible for the terminal’s upkeep and voicing his frustration over the state of the facilities.
He was also unhappy with the restrooms, pointing out that weeds were growing inside them even though users are charged a 50 sen entry fee.
His visit followed complaints and criticism from the public.

Title: Cable theft leaves 450 street lights in Putrajaya out of service, says Ahmad Maslan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 23 — Underground cable theft has been identified as the cause of 450 street lights along federal roads FT29 and FT30 in Putrajaya being out of service, said Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan.
He said the cable thefts occurred at the FT29/Maju Expressway (MEX) interchange, the FT29/FT30 interchange, the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) interchange, the Lebuh Gemilang interchange and the Lebuh Wadi Ehsan interchange.
“This is an enforcement issue when it comes to cable theft. Scrap metal dealers buy the stolen cables. If they do not buy them, there would be no incentive for people to sell or steal the cables.
“Therefore, action must be taken against both the cable thieves and those who buy stolen cables, and enforcement must be stepped up,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) on the maintenance status of street lights along FT29 and FT30, as well as plans to install solar-powered street lights, particularly at locations prone to cable theft, using a special allocation in 2027.
Ahmad said a total of 720 street lights along the two federal roads were not functioning, with other causes of damage including vehicle collisions and ageing infrastructure.
He said the Works Ministry had allocated RM840,000 in 2025 under the federal roads maintenance for Peninsular Malaysia for FT29 and FT30.
On the installation of solar-powered street lights, he said priority was given to areas prone to vandalism, villages and locations far from electricity supply networks.
“Each solar-powered street light costs RM10,000, while conventional street lights cost between RM4,000 and RM5,000 each. Conventional street lights are vulnerable to cable theft, while solar-powered street lights come with a five-year warranty compared with two years for conventional street lights.
Ahmad also urged Members of Parliament who wished to install solar-powered street lights in their respective constituencies to submit applications to the Works Ministry, with priority given to accident-prone areas. — Bernama

Title: Pahang open to data centres, but only in Gambang and Gebeng
Article:
KUANTAN, Nov 23 — Gambang and Gebeng here have been identified as the two locations with sufficient infrastructure, including land, water and electricity supply, as well as fibre optic connectivity, to support data centre development in Pahang.
Pahang Investment, Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Committee chairman Datuk Mohamad Nizar Najib said the state government would, however, closely scrutinise and monitor all data centre developments to ensure they did not affect electricity and water supplies for residents.
“We are not rejecting any applications for data centres, but we will approve them only in designated locations. For now, only Gambang and Gebeng have sufficient infrastructure.
“This is also being monitored at the Federal Government level through the Data Center Task Force... based on information received, the task force has decided that any new data centre development must generate at least 50 per cent of its electricity supply from its own sources,” he said.
He was replying to a supplementary question from Su Keong Siong (PH-Ketari) at the state assembly sitting here today on data centre development in the state.
Mohamad Nizar said applications for data centre development at the Federal Government level were currently facing lengthy waiting periods, with new projects expected to materialise only within the next one to two years.
Meanwhile, State Consumer Affairs and Human Resources Committee chairman Sim Chon Siang, in reply to Su’s question, said the MADANI Rahmah Sales Programme (PJRM) recorded sales exceeding RM66 million as at Oct 31 this year.
He said that apart from PJRM, the state government had also taken proactive steps to implement the ‘Jualan Makmur Kluster Perayaan’ programme as an additional initiative to complement Federal Government efforts to address the cost-of-living issue.
“For this purpose, the state government allocated RM2.52 million in 2025, and the programme received an encouraging response. Therefore, the allocation has been increased to RM7.56 million this year,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Johor sets aside RM3.8m to keep free medicine delivery service running in 2027
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 23 — The Johor state government has
allocated RM3.8 million to continue the free Medicine by Post (UMP) initiative
for all Johoreans next year, said State Health and Environment Committee
chairman Ling Tian Soon.
He said the allocation will benefit approximately 35,000
patients, with a target of serving 1,000 patients per month.
“Although the Communications Ministry had announced full
funding for the UMP service nationwide, the specific duration of the coverage
was not detailed.
“The state government has decided to maintain this
allocation because we do not want to gamble with the well-being of the people,
especially when it concerns their health,’ he said at the Johor state
legislative assembly in Kota Iskandar here today.
Ling was responding to a question from Datuk Ramlee Bohani
(BN-Kempas) regarding the UMP service in the state.
He noted that the state government began covering the
costs of the UMP service on August 1, 2024.
This initiative has benefited 101,035 patients, involving
504,294 medication parcels, with expenditures totalling RM1.34 million from
January to September 30 this year.
Ling, who is the Yong Peng assemblyman, added that the
remaining balance in the UMP trust account, amounting to RM838,910.80, is now
being utilised for the new ‘Same-Day Delivery’ initiative for
temperature-sensitive medications delivered by post.
The initiative, which began in September, was launched
with an initial allocation of RM49,500.
“This initiative, which involves six healthcare facilities
in the Johor Bahru district, has benefited 28 patients at a cost of RM420 in
September, with the figures subsequently rising to 74 patients at a cost of
RM1,110 in October.
“The six medical facilities involved are Sultanah Aminah
Hospital, Sultan Ismail Hospital, Pasir Gudang Hospital, as well as the Bukit
Indah, Kempas, and Pasir Gudang health clinics,” he said.
